Neque etiam tibi illud juxta hypothesis tuas licebit, qui id moliris, ut non actitatis insuper, nedum excitatis de Religione controversiis, omnes tacitè sopiantur, componantur, combinentur, puta ut V Veigelius solet docere suam Combinationem contradictoriorum, sub uno ac solo S. Scripturae verbo, & contextu mero, citra aliquam in diversas partes explicationem: nempe in Ecclesiâ tuâ conniventia, vel ut V Veigelius dicit, in mente. Quam ineptè, modò videbimus ubi ad ipsam causae disceptationem ventum erit, sententiam enim hactenus simpliciter eruimus. Tum, quidquid sit de verâ Ecclesiâ in specie, nostrâ, an qua alia, veram saltem hic in abstracto concipere, & praesupponere debemus, ubi de publico Novi Testamenti cultu tuam facis erotematicam propositionem, eamque Christianorum Ecclesiis, & caetibus illis, qui solam Veteris & Novi Testamenti scripturam pro unica fidei & morum Canone profitentur. II. Praemitto, Nos, ut Ecclesiam Reformatam, solam, nullam gentilicam, pro vera agnoscimus, & veneramur; ita pro ea, ejusque forma, & ministerio hic disputare, & de ea intelligi velle, quae pro Ecclesia a nobis afferentur. Itaque regredientes ad id quod propositum erat, ut ostenderem, scopum atque animum tibi hunc unice esse, publicum, qui obtinet in Ecclesia, Dei cultum abolere, & cum alio tuo commutare, vide pag. libelli tui 72. vel erotema clxxv I. & cxv I. quamvis hoc solum hic sufficerit, quod omnes Ecclesias Christianas censes esse apostaticas. Verum ut distinctius haec tractemus, quod non minimi laboris est, in rebus adeo confusis, & scripto taediosa corundem repetitione supra modum molesto; video quadruplicem tibi fingi Ecclesiam, vel Ecclesiae statum. I. Apostolicum, verum, quo verbum Euangelii infallibile ab Apostolis praedicatum, & Dei nomine fuit. II. Apostaticum, ab eo tempore usque, quo verbum non-infallibile, a ministris Ecclesiae fallibilibus concionatum & praedicatum tamen nomine Dei fuit. III. Commitentia, hoc tuo tempore, & per te, si sanis placet, erigendum, in hoc temporis interstitio quasi, & apostasiae periodo, sub Dei offensione, ad IV. Apostolicum iterum, quo pristinus & infallibiliter concionantium ordo Ecclesiaeque status iterum reducetur, credo, quando Elias veniet. 1P n.
units.tr: I have said, then, that you wish everything in the Churches changed, indeed overturned, especially what pertains to the common and customary manner of preaching. Therefore, for the sake of a better order and a necessary method, I first set out two things which pertain to the subject of the controversy and to your opinion. 1. I presuppose in this question that the Churches are true as regards doctrine; otherwise, who would doubt that false and heretical churches, with all their sermons and ministry, must be abolished and cursed? So understand that the sermons in the Churches are true, sounding the true doctrine of Christ and the apostles. If you deny that these are anywhere in the world, or indeed that they are ours, then no dispute about the form of preaching, the ministry and divine worship, which we carry on not as infallible yet in God's name, will need to be instituted between us. Rather, the heads of doctrine will have to be taken up, and a suit about them brought by you against us, together with our other adversaries; and there you too will stand with the rest of the Achaeans in one rank. Nor, according to your hypotheses, will it be permitted to you, who strive to bring it about that controversies about religion are silently lulled, settled and combined, not only without being stirred up but even without being excited. V. Veigelius usually teaches this, with his combination of contradictories under the one and sole word of Holy Scripture and mere context, without any explanation into different parts: namely, in your Church, connivance, or, as V. Veigelius says, in the mind. How clumsily this is done we shall see when we come to the very argument of the cause; for hitherto we have only drawn out your opinion. Then, whatever may be the case about the true Church in particular, ours or some other, we must conceive and presuppose a true one here in the abstract, since you make your erotematic proposition about the public worship of the New Testament, and aim that proposition at "the Churches of Christians and those assemblies which profess the Scripture of the Old and New Testament alone as the sole canon of faith and morals." II. I premise that we, as the Reformed Church, acknowledge and venerate only it as true, and no Gentile church; and so we wish to dispute here, and to be understood, concerning it, its form and its ministry, and concerning what is put forward by us as the Church. Returning, then, to what was proposed: to show that your sole aim and purpose is to abolish the public worship of God which obtains in the Church, and to exchange it for another of yours, see page 72 of your pamphlet, or erotemas 175 and 115. Yet here it will suffice that you judge all Christian churches to be apostate. But to treat these matters more distinctly, which is no small labour given such confused matters and a writing tiresome beyond measure through its tedious repetition, I see that you imagine a fourfold Church, or state of the Church. I. The apostolic, true, in which the infallible gospel word preached by the apostles was held in God's name. II. The apostate, from the time when the non-infallible word, preached by fallible ministers of the Church, was nevertheless proclaimed in God's name. III. The connivent, to be erected in your time, and by you, if it pleases the sane, in this interval, as it were, and period of apostasy, under the displeasure of God. IV. The apostolic again, in which the earlier order of infallibly preaching men and the state of the Church will be restored, I believe, when Elijah comes.

units.la: De singulis necesse habemus mentem tuam attentius examinare, sed & praemittere explicationis causa, nonnulla: I. de verbo, quod praedicatur, infallibili. II. de modo quo id praedicatur, vel, quo pacto, Dei nomine: etenim non erro, si dixero ab hisce duobus pendere omne molimen tui negotii, & erotematum, & ab hisce
units.tr: We must examine your mind more attentively on each point. But first, for the sake of explanation, we must premise a few things: I. concerning the word which is preached as infallible; II. concerning the manner in which it is preached, or how it is preached in God's name. For I am not wrong if I say that the whole effort of your business and your erotemas depends on these two, and that moves on them as on hinges

units.la: { } bisce quasi axibus novum tuum & totum orbem moveri.
units.tr: as on hinges, your whole new world is moved.

units.la: Valdè hoc in Ecclesiis reprehendis, quod ibi praedicatur non verbum ὅλως infitè, indubiè mereque verum: sed praeter S. scripturam, verbum non eo gradu verum, fallibile. Primò satis illa est impedita ac molesta loquendi ratio, qua vel centies, si non ultra in hoc brevi scripto, singulis ferè erotematis intellectum lectoris iterum iterumque divexas, isthoc tuo verbo ὅλως infitè, indubiè, mereque vero; dic uno verbo, infallibili: annon id commodius & intelligibilius? etiam ad leges disputandi accuratius? atque sic omne dixi, & nervosius quam tu tot semper incassum repetitis epithetis: quid ὅλως, quod est totaliter, ὁλως infitè, indubiè, mereque verum? an aliud, quam quod infallibile dicimus? & quod infallibile, annon hoc tale, ut ὅλως, infitè, indubiè, mereque verum sit? si enim βατραχομυομαχίας agere constitutum tibi, iisque libellum farcire, plura etiam synonyma vel epithéta connectere hoc in sermone potuisses. Imò, quod secundò noto, infallibile plus videtur dicere, quam tuum ὅλως infitè, indubiè, mereque verum, hoc enim dicitur, quod in se tale est, ut neutiquam fallat; illud verò non modo hoc, sed respectum insuper hoc in negotio & rationem ad ipsum Auctorem infallibilem, sive infallibiliter docentem, ut non materialiter solùm indubium sit, sed & formaliter. Vt, verbum Apostolorum similiumque, qualium verbum in verâ concione & Ecclesiâ solum audiri vis, est non modò in se materialiter infitè, indubiè, mereque verum; sed à talibus prolatum, qui errare, ut ipse agnoscis, nec poterant, neque volebant, atque hoc est, infallibilibus. Verbi gratia, quidni possem ego proferre, vel etiam tu bone vir, verbum aliquod infitè, indubiè, mereque verum? neque tamen nos, saltem ego nolim verbum meum, quatenus à me procedit, haberi infallibile. Nisi quando indubiè dicis, tantundem intelligas, ac infalfallibile: quamvis & hoc indubie, videatur sonare actualem duntaxat & materialem veritatem, infallibile etiam cum respectu, ut diximus, ad Auctorem, verbum quod non potest non esse verissimum. Quidquid sit, vel indubium dicere verbum, sufficeret; vel (ut de vocibus ulteriorem nullam litem moveam) quando ego in hac de concione verbi controversia, simpliciter dico verbum infallibile, scias tum me exprimere brevius, quod tu tanto verborum apparatu. Videlicet, ipse quoque sive erotem. VI. non aliter tua explicas unicum solum ac individuum illud verbum Christi promissum ἅλως infite indubie mereque verum, cujus insitus scilicet ac indubius character, est omnis vel minimi erroris qualiscunque carentia, ac veritas, id est, infallibile: & alibi erot. CVII, indubie mereque, verum explicas per authenticum & erot. IX. per ἀψεύδεως III. Praemitto eam, quae ex dictis jam fere liquet, & in sequentibus multi usus erit, distinctionem inter verum & infallibile: aliud, verum; aliud, quod insuper infallibile. Veri Doctores quidem sumus, at non infallibiles. IV. Infallibiles Doctores habent ad docendum immediatam & extraordinariam vocationem: qui vero simpliciter Doctores veritatis sint jam ita traditae infallibiliter ab extraordinarie & immediate vocatis, iis sufficit ordinaria & mediata vocatio. Primis ergo veritatis Evangelicae praeconibus necessaria quidem fuit immediata atque extraordinaria vocatio, ad extraordinarium doctrinae infallibilis negotium; sed eo dato, jam veritas secundum eam solum quaeritur ordinarie: ideoque infallibiles, vel immediate, aut extraordinarie missos Concionatores non est quod exigamus, vel praestolemur. Alterum, de quo explicationis causa nonnihil praemittendum duxi, est de modo, forma, vel nomine, quo conciones in Ecclesiis habentur, quid sit nomine Dei concionari? nomine Dei varie aliquid dicitur fieri, vel quoque in nomen Dei, ὁ ἰδόμενος, & εἰς ὄνομα, ΟΩ I. ex nomine, ut sic loquar, Dei, i.e. Dei jussu, mandato, atque authoritate. Matth. xxi. 23. quâ potestate hæc facis, & τίνι ἐξουσίᾳ? vel quis tibi dedit hanc potestatem? adde vers. 25. Iohan. v. 43. Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, & non recipitis me: quod si alius venerit in proprio nomine, illum recipietis. 1. Cor. v. 4. Deinde in nomine Dei, significat, per Deum, vel cum Deo, ejus ope, auxilio, sub ejus ductu fieri. 1. Sam. xvii. 45. Tu venis ad me cum gladio, & cum hasta, & cum humeralis; ego vero venio ad te in nomine Iehova exercituum. Psalm. xx. 6. & in nomine Dei nostri vexillis extollemur. adde vers. 8. Marc. xvi. 17. Signa vero fideles haec sequentur: in nomine meo daemonia ejicient. Luc. ix. 49. Tertiò, in nomine Dei, est propter Deum, ejus causa, &, ut solemus dicere, gratia. Luc. ix. 48. quicunque receperit hunc puerulum in nomine meo, me recipit. adde vers. 49. & Matth. x. 41. 42. & xviii. 5. Ioan. xiv. 13. Et quodcunque in nomine meo petieritis, hoc faciam. & vers. 14. 26. Vltimò, in nomine vel in nomen Dei, & Christi, est in ipsum Deum, ac Christum. Et in nomine ipsius sperabunt gentes. Matth. xii. 21. Matth. xxviii. 19. baptizantes eos in nomen Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: You criticise it sharply in the churches that what is preached there is not a word that is wholly [ὅλως] undoubted and truly true, but apart from Holy Scripture a word that is not true to that degree and is fallible. First, that way of speaking is awkward and burdensome. In this short writing you vex the reader's understanding again and again, perhaps a hundred times or more, in almost every question, with that phrase of yours: wholly [ὅλως], undeniably, unquestionably, and truly true. Say it in one word: infallible. Is that not more convenient and more intelligible, and also more exact by the rules of disputation? That way I have said everything, and more forcefully than you, who keep repeating so many epithets to no purpose. What is "wholly [ὅλως], undeniably, unquestionably, truly true," other than what we call infallible? And is not the infallible the very thing that is wholly, undeniably, unquestionably, and truly true? If you intended to wage a battle of frogs and mice [βατραχομυομαχίας] and stuff your little book with words, you could have strung together even more synonyms or epithets in this discourse. Indeed, and this is my second point, infallible seems to say more than your "wholly [ὅλως], undeniably, unquestionably, truly true." The latter says only that a thing is such in itself that it can by no means deceive. The former says not only this, but also includes a relation and reference, in this matter, to the infallible Author himself, or to one who teaches infallibly, so that it is undeniable not merely materially but also formally. Thus the word of the apostles and of similar men, the kind of word you wish to be heard only in a true sermon and in the Church, is not only in itself materially undeniable, unquestionable, and truly true, but was uttered by men who, as you yourself acknowledge, could not err, nor did they want to; and this is what makes it infallible. For example, why could I not utter some word, or you too, good sir, that is undeniably, unquestionably, and truly true? Yet we, at least I, would not wish my word, insofar as it proceeds from me, to be held infallible. Unless, when you say undoubted, you mean exactly the same as infallible, although this word undoubted seems to signify only actual and material truth, whereas infallible, as I said, also has reference to the Author, being a word that cannot fail to be most true. Whatever the case, it would have been enough to call the word undoubted, or (so as not to raise any further dispute over words) when I, in this controversy about the preaching of the Word, simply say that the word is infallible, you should know that I express it more briefly than you with your great array of words. Indeed, you yourself in question VI explain that unique and single word of Christ, promised, wholly [ὅλως], undeniably, and truly true, whose inherent and undoubted character is the lack of any, even the smallest, error of any kind, and its truth; that is, infallible. And elsewhere, in question CVII, you explain "undeniably, truly" by "authentic," and in question IX by "without deceit" [ἀψεύδεως] in III. I shall premise the distinction, which is already almost clear from what has been said and will be of much use in what follows, between true and infallible: one thing is true, another is in addition infallible. We are indeed true teachers, but not infallible ones. IV. Infallible teachers have an immediate and extraordinary calling to teach. But those who are simply teachers of a truth already so handed down infallibly by the extraordinarily and immediately called are satisfied with an ordinary and mediate calling. So the first heralds of the Gospel truth did indeed need an immediate and extraordinary calling, for the extraordinary task of an infallible teaching. But once that has been given, truth is now sought ordinarily according to that teaching alone; therefore we need not demand or wait for preachers who are infallible, or who have been sent immediately or extraordinarily. The other matter, which I thought should be premised for the sake of explanation, concerns the manner, form, or name in which sermons are given in the churches: what does it mean to preach in the name of God? Something is said to be done in the name of God in various ways, or also into the name of God [ὁ ἰδόμενος], and into the name [εἰς ὄνομα]. First, from the name, as I may put it, of God, that is, by God's command, order, and authority. Matt. 21:23: "By what authority [ἐξουσίᾳ] do you do these things? or who gave you this authority?" Add verse 25. John 5:43: "I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me; if another comes in his own name, you will receive him." 1 Cor. 5:4. Secondly, in the name of God means by God, or with God, done with his help, aid, and under his guidance. 1 Sam. 17:45: "You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts." Ps. 20:6: "And in the name of our God we will lift up our banners." Add verse 8. Mark 16:17: "And these signs will follow those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons." Luke 9:49. Thirdly, in the name of God means for God's sake, on his account, and, as we usually say, for the sake of his grace. Luke 9:48: "Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me." Add verse 49, and Matt. 10:41-42, and 18:5. John 14:13: "And whatever you ask in my name, I will do it." And verses 14 and 26. Lastly, in the name or into the name of God and of Christ means into God himself and Christ. Matt. 12:21: "And in his name the Gentiles will hope." Matt. 28:19: "baptizing them into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit."

units.la: 1. Cor. i. 12. 13. Vt nomen Dei est ipse Deus [illegible, ~4 letters] [illegible, ~4 letters]. Noster, nomine Dei solet exponere, Dei loco & authoritate, seu tanquam pro Deo legatione fungi, & Dei personam sustinere, erot. ix. & per totum. In quo hoc quidem non negamus, illum qui sic Dei loco, authoritate, pro Deo legatione fungens, reique personam sustinens aliquid agit, quin verè dicatur nomine Dei agere, quamvis & eo sensu illud Dei nomine in N. Test. non occurrat, quod tamen attendere hoc in casu debuisset, quem adeo fundamentalem ad cultum N. Test. facit, sed negamus ei, non posse dici quid nomine Dei agi vel fieri, nisi quod sic peculiariter Dei loco, &c. geratur: tum etiam, quod qui Dei nomine quid dicitur agere, exponi debeat infallibiliter tamquam ab ipso Deo, (quod vult erot. ix.) fieri, ve-
units.tr: 1 Cor. 1:12-13. As the name of God is God himself [illegible, about four letters] [illegible, about four letters]. Our author usually explains in the name of God as in the place of God and by his authority, or as one who acts as God's legate in place of God, and sustains the person of God, question IX and throughout. In this we do not deny that one who thus acts in the place of God, by his authority, as God's legate, and sustains the person of the one he represents, does something that may truly be said to be done in the name of God, although in that sense the phrase in the name of God does not occur in the New Testament, which he ought to have considered in this case, since he makes it so fundamental to the worship of the New Testament. But we deny that it can be said that anything is done or made in the name of God unless it is carried out in this particular way, in the place of God, etc. Moreover, we deny that whoever is said to act in the name of God must be explained as doing it infallibly, as from God himself (which question IX wants), and the same applies to

units.la: { } Catchword "quo" at the lower right, outside the text. quoque, qui Dei loco, & authoritate quid agit, quod id merè divinum ac indubium & infallibile ideo sit. V. g. Magistratus & principes, nunquid Dii dicuntur אלהים? Psal. lxxxii. 1. 6. annon Dei personam sustinent? Rom. xiii. 1. Dei nomine, loco, & authoritate justitiam administrant? errare tamen possunt: unde vides, non sequi, ut quis dici possit Dei nomine sive loco & authoritate agere, necesse esse, ut non aliter quam ὡς ἂν insitè indubiè mereque verè, σὺν ψυχῇ & infallibiliter agat. Sic quoque ministri N. Test. nomine Dei dicuntur habere suas ex verbo Dei conciones: nec tamen sequitur debere eas esse merè infallibiles, alioqui nec nomine Dei habendas, vel accipiendas.
units.tr: [Catchword "quo" at the lower right, outside the text.] who acts in the place of God and by his authority, so that what he does is purely divine, undoubted, and infallible. For example, are magistrates and princes not called gods, elohim [אלהים]? Ps. 82:1, 6. Do they not sustain the person of God? Rom. 13:1. Do they not administer justice in the name, place, and authority of God? Yet they can err. From this you see that it does not follow that, for someone to be said to act in the name, or in the place and authority, of God, he must necessarily act only as one who is undeniably, unquestionably, truly, and infallibly acting [σὺν ψυχῇ] with his whole soul. So also the ministers of the New Testament are said to have their sermons from the Word of God in the name of God, yet it does not follow that these must be purely infallible; otherwise they would not be held or received as being in the name of God.

units.la: Hisce praemissis, ad Authorem nostrum me verto, & explicari ab ipso peto quadruplicem illam, quam ex ejus sententiâ propositi, Ecclesiam. Primam autem & Apostolicam explicat, ut video, à libelli pag. 5. ad 25. sive ab cap. VII. usque ad XVIII. Et primam illam, ac genuinam Evangelii praedicationem per Johannem Baptistam, per ipsum Dominum ac Apostolos ejus peractam dicit. Benè, non quaeram, an doctrinam Johannis, cum eâ, quae Christi Apostolorumque, substantialiter eandem faciat? quia id satis videtur affirmari. Caeterum quia non ignorat, saltem ignorare non debet, à Papistis, Socinianis, atque Anabaptistis, illud negari, observari obiter volo, quam frustra nostri homines moliantur omnium sectarum syncretismum, sub nudis S. scripturae verbis; quum adeo nihil dici possit, quam manifestissimae etiam in S. scripturâ sit veritatis, quod non alium pungat statim, & adversarium suum reperiat, neque possibile est Scripturam legere & audire, ut non aliquam ejus apud te, etiam apud alium facias intelligentiam atque expositionem, facilè controversam. Sed ad Apostolos, eorumque praedicationem, quam infallibilem, & Dei nomine habitam fuisse, extra dubium est, De particularium Ecclesiarum ævo Ajo-
units.tr: Having premised these things, I turn to our author and ask him to explain that fourfold church which, by his account, he has in view. He explains the first, which is the Apostolic church, as I see it, from page 5 to page 25 of his pamphlet, that is, from chapter VII to chapter XVIII. He says that this first and genuine preaching of the Gospel was carried out by John the Baptist, by the Lord himself, and by his Apostles. Well and good. I will not ask whether the doctrine of John is substantially the same as that of Christ and the Apostles, since that seems sufficiently affirmed. But since he does not, or at least should not, be unaware that the Papists, the Socinians and the Anabaptists deny this, I wish to observe in passing how vainly our people labour to effect a syncretism of all the sects under the bare words of Holy Scripture. Nothing can be said, however manifest the truth in Holy Scripture may be, that does not at once prick someone else and find its opponent; nor is it possible to read or hear Scripture without making some interpretation and exposition of it, which is easily disputed. But as for the Apostles and their preaching, which is beyond doubt infallible and was held to be given in God's name, I come to the age of the particular churches, which begins at Ezek. xi.

units.la: Slostolica ministris, incipit Ezech. xı. & bene est quod illos consentiat fallibiles fuisse, & datos etiam à Christo, in quo eos ab Apostolis, qui à verbi veritate deflectere nec poterant nec volebant, distinguit, quia deflectere imò poterant, & aliqui eorum etiam deflectebant, ibid. xı. utcunque illis particularium Ecclesiarum ministris fallibilibus hoc eodem erotemate & seq. xıv. xv. xvı. xvıı. concedat cum Apostolis, quod idem & infallibile Christi verbum, Dei etiam nomine Ecclesiis, ad quod à Deo primùm & dati & donis instructi fuerunt, prædicarent; sed dicit, personas tantum eâ in re ab invicem discrepasse, quod Apostoli infallibiles, hi verò fallibiles essent, & à verbi veritate deficere poterant: unde argumentum contra ejus sententiam, verbum Dei infallibile etiam à fallibilibus exponi & prædicari, Dei nomine, posse; neque hoc quando fit, apostaticum dici debere, vel Ecclesiarum Christianarum apostasiam inde derivari, quod verbum prædicatorium, ut loquitur, sive verbi divini conciones habeantur à non-infallibilibus, & Dei tamen nomine, quomodo verbum illorum orale, quà illorum, cùm Apostolico infallibili æquiparari nequit. Sed hoc latius exponemus posteà, ubi contra sententiam ejus argumenta afferemus nostra. Interim ibid. xıı ı. ait, fideli populo ex illâ nonnullorum ministrorum defectione nil periculi fuisse, quia populus ille ævi τὸ χρίσμα ἀ ψεῦδος ἀλλ' ἀλήθεια habet, & veritatem nosset (1 Ioan. 2. vers. 20, 21.), & quæ ibi porrò accumulat: sed, an non illa omnis ævi populus Christianus quoque habet? nonne illa semper in fidelibus vera, illisque competunt, quæ ibi longo ordine recenseт privilegia, & dona piorum? annon etiam populus, æquè ac ministri istius ævi, deficere à veritate poterat, & non animadvertere, utrum & quinam particulares ministri à verbi illius puritate deflecterent? quo ergo fine dicit, populo isti tamen nil periculi esse potuisse, à defectione ac apostasiâ suorum ministrorum.
units.tr: (The Apostolic ministers were distinguished from the ministers of the particular churches.) He is right that these latter were fallible, and that they were given by Christ, from whom he distinguishes them, as the Apostles, who could not and would not depart from the truth of the Word, were not. For these ministers could indeed depart from it, and some of them did depart, Ezek. xi. Yet he concedes, under this same heading and in the following chapters, Ezek. xiv, xv, xvi, xvii, that together with the Apostles they preached the same infallible Word of Christ, and also in God's name, to the churches, to which they were first given and equipped with gifts by God. But he says that the persons alone differed in this respect: the Apostles were infallible, while these were fallible and could fall away from the truth of the Word. Hence my argument against his view: the infallible Word of God can be expounded and preached in God's name even by fallible men; and when this happens it ought not to be called apostasy, nor should the apostasy of Christian churches be derived from the fact that the preaching word, as he calls it, or sermons of the divine Word, are delivered by non-infallible men, yet in God's name, since their oral word, as theirs, cannot be equated with the infallible Apostolic word. But I shall explain this more fully later, when I set out my arguments against his view. Meanwhile, at Ezek. xii, he says that the faithful people suffered no danger from the defection of some ministers, because that people had "the anointing, which is not a lie but the truth" [τὸ χρίσμα ... ἀλλ' ἀλήθεια] and knew the truth (1 John 2:20, 21), and what he piles up further there. But does not every Christian people of every age have this too? Are not those privileges and gifts of the godly, which he recounts there in a long list, always true in believers and fitting for them? Could not the people of every age, just as the ministers of that age, depart from the truth and fail to notice whether, and which, particular ministers were turning aside from the purity of that Word? To what end, then, does he say that this people could nevertheless suffer no danger from the defection and apostasy of their ministers?

units.la: Progrediamur ab Ecclesia Apostolica, ad Apostaticam, quae brevissimo ab Apostolis intervallo ex tuo judicio inceperit, & hucusque talis, juxta opinionem tuam duravit, in eo tandem felix, quod per te demum cognoscat, quam neutiquam sit id quod hactenus visa fuit esse, & quomodo hinc etiam ad non minus mutilam & imperfectam conniventia conditionem, te si sequi constituerit, pervenire possit. Hanc non unius, alterius ve Ecclesiae, vel quod majus, saeculi unius apostasiam criminaris, sed omnium & quarumcunque per orbem universum quae sunt, & ulterius, quae a temporibus Apostolorum usque, & a primis Ecclesiae initiis fuerunt, Ecclesiarum statum defectivum, & iniquitatis plenum arguis: nempe ut eo audacius appareat facinus, quo non in unum hostem, vel unam Ecclesiam incurrere satis, vel forte operae pretium videtur, nisi universum Christianismum, & omnes ejus Ecclesias simul eodemque furore evertas. Capua tu legiones dissipavisti spiritu, quasi ventus folia, aut pannicalam sectariam.
units.tr: Let us pass from the Apostolic church to the apostate church, which, by your judgment, began after a very short interval from the Apostles, and has lasted until now according to your opinion; happy in this at last, that through you it may learn how far from what it has hitherto seemed to be it truly is, and how, from this point, it may also come, if you resolve to follow, to a condition of connivance no less mutilated and imperfect. You accuse not one church or another, or, what is greater, the apostasy of one age, but of all and whatever churches there are throughout the whole world, and further, of the defective and iniquity-filled state of the churches which have existed from the times of the Apostles and from the first beginnings of the Church. You do this so that the deed may appear the more audacious, since it seems scarcely worth the trouble to attack one enemy or one church, unless you overthrow all of Christianity and all its churches at once and with the same fury. You have scattered the legions of Capua with your spirit, like the wind scatters leaves, or a sectarian rag.

units.la: Ita quippe erat. xxiv. dicis a primis Novi Testamenti initiis hoc incepisse in Ecclesia, in quo ejus apostasiam, & mysterium iniquitatis collocas: qui praecipuum Novi Testamenti cultum, a primis ejus initiis, & deinceps, Dei st dictum est nomine administrant, non prout Deus cum nomine suo administrari vult, etc. Itaque, jam statim a primis Nov. Test. initiis corrupta & apostatica Ecclesia, & deinceps, hucusque per tot secula? sic vera non fuit, nisi valde exiguo tempore Ecclesia; non sane diutius, quam Apostoli eam docuerunt, imo & ante Apostolorum excessum, quando sc. particularium Ecclesiarum ministri inceperunt deficere a puritate verbi divini, quod etiam juxta erat. xii. vel praesentibus Apostolis contigit, ergo jam tum coepit apostatica esse Ecclesia. Ea, quam egregia sic nobis Ecclesia Christiana depingitur? quam ea nulla fere unquam fuit, haec si vera sint? & quot animarum myriades deceptae, tot claelapsis seculis, quae ex Gentilismo, vel Iudaismo, aut variis haeresibus ad Ecclesiam Christianam imponendo studio ac zelo converse, & catervatim ad eam semper concurrerunt, ut ad veram Ecclesiam, & salutis suae sacratissimam anchoram! quam falsi fideles omnes, qui hactenus credere jussi, unam, veram, sanctam Ecclesiam Catholicam? sed insuper tuum hoc de omni catholica Ecclesia a primis ejus initiis apostatica laevum judicium audiamus: erot. cxx. vel pag. 54. Ecclesiam dicis, a primis predicationis sue initiis, & deinceps, verbo orali destitutam fuisse, quae Evangelium primitus nomine Dei inchoatum & institutum fuit, &c. atque hoc tibi mysterium iniquitatis & apostasiae: egregie sane. Hinc tua illa & passim usitata phrasi Ecclesias apostaticas fuisse dicis ab avo, hodieque, id est, a primis ejus initiis, sicut jam explicuisti erot. lxiii. utrum, ab avo, hodieque, &c. sic & erot. xcviii. cx. cxlviii. cl. Titulus, quibus hunc perpetuum Ecclesiae statum insignis & describis, sunt; cultum ejus voluntarium, & ἐθελοθρησκείας fuisse, erot. xxiv. xxvi. xxviii. Deinde, imperfectum ac praesumtuosum, erot. cliv. pro imperfecta quidem, quia inter alia ministri eorum destituuntur verbo orali ὡς insite indubie mereque vero, quod Dei nomine in publico suo cultu proferant: pro praesumtuosa autem, quia nihilominus verbum suum concionatorium non ὡς insite indubie mereque verum, loco verbi ἄλλης insite indubie mereque veri, quod Dei ut dictum est nomine, publico incultu unice proferri debet, substituunt. hoc falsum, nos verbum nostrum concionatorium, qua nostrum, loco verbi divini substituere. mendacissimum, quod vehementer miror alicui excidere potuisse in Ecclesia nostra enutrito, & studiis nostris saltem hactenus imbuto, illud ut ignorare haud debuerit. De coetibus nostris, ex ejus sententia imperfectis, & praesumtuosis itidem erot. clviii. Tum Ecclesias, a primis praedicati Euangelii initiis, apostaticas appellat, erot. cxx. Vitium in parte talia [illegible, ~20 letters] ecclesia cum ratione negare possit se recessisse aut defecisse à primæva illâ Christi quoad verbum promissum institutione, Ecclesiarumque per id juxta illam nomine Dei seu pro-Deo legatione fungendo, erectione, collectione & regimine, atque eatenus (de promisso autem spiritu id suo etiam loco probabitur) apostaticam esse. Obiter, quid sibi illud vult quoad verbum promissum institutione? explica distincte, quod verbum intelligas, quamque ejus institutionem. Et erot. cxlvi. ecclesiam apostaticam dicit. Erot. xciii. mysterium iniquitatis: nempe hoc vult, ab ævo, hodieque, sive à primis prædicati Euangelii initiis, Ecclesias omnes Christianas apostaticas sub mysterio iniquitatis fuisse, juxta descriptionem apostasiæ Antichristianæ. II Thess.
units.tr: Indeed it was so. xxiv. You say that this began in the Church from the first beginnings of the New Testament, and in it you place its apostasy and the mystery of iniquity: they administer the principal worship of the New Testament, from its first beginnings and onward, in the name of God, which has been said, not as God wishes to be administered in his own name, etc. So then, from the very first beginnings of the New Testament the Church was corrupt and apostate, and onward, down to the present, through so many centuries? Thus the Church would have been true only for a very short time, certainly no longer than the Apostles taught it; indeed, even before the Apostles' departure, when the ministers of the particular churches began to fall away from the purity of the divine Word, which, according to xii, happened even while the Apostles were present. Therefore the Church was already apostate at that time. What a splendid picture of the Christian Church you paint for us! If these things are true, when has the Church ever been anything but almost nonexistent? And how many myriads of souls, deceived over so many centuries, who were converted to the Christian Church from Gentilism, Judaism, or various heresies, and who with eagerness and zeal have always flocked to it in crowds as to the true Church and the most sacred anchor of their salvation! How false are all the faithful who have hitherto been bidden to believe in one, true, holy, catholic Church! But let us hear further your left-handed judgment of every catholic Church, apostate from its first beginnings: at question cxx, or page 54, you say the Church, from the first beginnings of its preaching and onward, was destitute of the oral word, which was first begun and established in God's name, etc. And this you call the mystery of iniquity and apostasy: very splendid indeed. Hence, in that phrase of yours, used everywhere, you say the churches have been apostate from the beginning, even today, that is, from its first beginnings, as you have already explained at question lxiii, where you say from the beginning, even today, etc. So also at questions xcviii, cx, cxlviii and cl. The titles by which you mark and describe this perpetual state of the Church are that its worship was voluntary and [ἐθελοθρησκείας] self-chosen, at questions xxiv, xxvi and xxviii. Then, imperfect and presumptuous, at question cliv: imperfect indeed, because among other things their ministers lack the oral word, which they should profess in public worship in God's name as indubitably and purely true; but presumptuous, because nevertheless they put in place of the word which is to be professed in public worship, in God's name as has been said, their own preaching word, not as indubitably and purely true. This is false: we do not substitute our preaching word, as ours, for the divine Word. It is most mendacious, and I am greatly surprised that anyone reared in our Church, and at least hitherto steeped in our studies, could have let it slip, since he ought not to have been ignorant of it. Concerning our assemblies, which by his judgment are imperfect and presumptuous, likewise at question clviii. Then he calls the churches apostate from the first beginnings of the preaching of the Gospel, at question cxx. A fault in part such [illegible, about 20 letters] … the church cannot reasonably deny that it has withdrawn or fallen away from that primal institution of Christ with regard to the promised Word, and from the erection, gathering and governing of churches by that Word, and so, to that extent, is apostate. (That it has the promised Spirit will be proved in its own place.) Incidentally, what does he mean by "the institution with regard to the promised Word"? Explain distinctly which Word you mean, and what its institution is. And at question cxlvi he calls the church apostate. At question xciii, the mystery of iniquity. He means this: from the beginning, even today, or from the first beginnings of the preached Gospel, all Christian churches have been apostate under the mystery of iniquity, according to the description of Antichristian apostasy in 2 Thess. 2. On the apostate church the author sets out his mind at pages 26 to 32, repeats it at pages 38 and 55, and in those two passages, almost, he lays down the foundation and the crime of apostasy under formal reasons. I. Because not only in sermons and in the public worship of God...

units.la: 2. De Ecclesiâ apostaticâ mentem suam promit Auctor, pag. 26. ad 32. repetit p. 38. & 55. atque in illis fere duobus, ut formalibus rationibus apostasiæ fundamentum, ac crimen ponit. I. Quòd non unicè in concionibus & cultu Dei publico in Ecclesiis audiatur verbum θεοῦ divinum, ac infallibile, sed verbum Dei Vet. ac Novi Test. ῥῆμα divinum, ac infallibile exponatur, tractetur, prædicetur verbo hominum non infallibilium, haud æquè divino & infallibili, ac est verbum S. Scripturæ. II. Quòd tamen verbum illud concionum in Ecclesiis dicatur habere nomine, & authoritate Dei. Idcóque, quod inde sequitur, & ceu tertium sit advertas, ex erot. clxv. non ab omnibus & quibusvis promiscuè, sed à certis in Ecclesiâ ad id vocatis, ac instructis ministris tractari. In illis hæret cardo omnis controversiæ, quam nobis movet, omneque sententiæ ejus momentum: illa exagitat in Ecclesiis nostris, neque nostris solùm, sed omnibus, quotquot nomen Christianum ferunt, sive quæ ab ævo hodièque, i. e. à temporibus Apostolorum in orbe fuerunt: illa criminatur, condemnat: hic ei mysterium iniquitatis, apostasia, cultus falsus, & antichristiana quæque apparent. Nimiùm quam tumultuatur. exclamat, monet, minatur, & da pedem figere, vel terram super bis, sc motorum indicat. Erat. XXII. Quaerendum est, utrum igitur illi, qui non exstante Dei in S. S. literis hac de re mandato, institutione, aut beneplacita permissione, nihilominus tamen geminam illam debitamque Evangelii praedicationem, duntaxat verbo illo ἄλως insitè indubiè mereque vero Dei ut dictum est nomine primitus inchoatam & institutam continuant nomine Dei, id est, Dei loco & authoritate, seu tanquam pro Deo legatione fungendo, sive conscie, sive insciè, verbo ut dictum est non ὁ ἄλως insitè indubiè mereque vero: item qui similiter Evangelii praedicationem ullam, Dei nomine seu tanquam pro Deo legatione fungentes, sive conscie, sive insciè primitus inchoant, continuant & instituunt, & peragunt, verbo ut dictum est non ὁ ἄλως insitè indubiè mereque vero; ut cum inquam illi eo ipso, eadem praedicationis Evangelii administrent, prout Deus eam nomine suo administrari vult; qui autem eo ipso illam administrent, prout ipsis bonum videtur, ipsique volunt? Quibus verborum ampullis, inani corundem circuitione, periphrasi, repetitione rem nihili, vel facile & verbulo absolvendam agis, id est, magno cornato magnas nugas? Hoc vis quaeri: Utrum, qui Dei nomine praedicationem Evangelii continuant, tamen verbo & concione non omnino & sic infallibili, ac ipsum est Evangelium, praedicationem illam administrent, prout docet, vel prout eam Deus exerceri vult? quorsum tot verba, otiosa epitheta, repetitio per item? & tam tortuose propositia controversia? ubi semel explicuisti, quale verbum infallibile in concionibus publicis postules, quod appellas ἄλως insitè indubiè mereque verum, quorsum idem ad nauseam usque & mentis turbandam attentionem quolibet iterum paragrapho repetitum? Si semel expositum, quid nomine Dei, quod proponi debeat, intelligendum existimes; eccur totics illud idemque inaniter redit, Dei nomine, id est, Dei loco, & authoritate seu tanquam pro Deo, &c. Et super hisce duobus, ut ex hoc aliisque erotemais liquet, tota veritas con controversia, verbo Dei infallibili, atque nomine Dei habendo. ergo. Ⅲ. i. cl. iv. & prius illud quia in Ecclesiis ab hominibus non continuatur, ecclesias appellat imperfectas; & quia tamen aliquem adhibent id est Dei nomine nihilominus concionés habent, ideo eas appellat presumtuosas: quae item duo ea sunt, ex quibus videtur nasci Ecclesiarum omnium Christianarum nam omnium hic similis casus, apostasia. Erotematis vel articulo XVIII, pag. 25. dicit in Monito, verum controversiae statum luculentissime signatum: Videamus ergo: sic ibidem loquitur: Imprimis quaerendum est, utrum Deus aliquibus in S. scriptura illis Ecclesiae suae ministris aliisve mandaverit, aut beneplacite permiserit, ut genuina illa debitaque Evangelii praedicatio, quae Dei nomine, id est, loco & authoritate Dei, seu pro Deo legatione fungendo, primitus inchoata (ut dictum est) & instituta a Deo sunt, duntaxat verbo illo Christi promissio ὅλως insite indubie mereque vero, omnino scilicet insitè ut διαφθορᾷ, ὀρεῖ, ἀχαλαγαστῳ, in aeternum manens, & de quo tota quantum quantum erat indubie verèque dici poterat, verbum tuum est veritas, videlicet, quod & ὅλως insitè indubie mereque verum erat, & de quo tum ipsi, qui id praedicabant, tum qui illud jam ut dictum est receperant, perinde ac de ipsissimo Dei verbo ὅλως insitè indubie mereque vero, ἀψευδῶς persuasi esse poterant, & erant; ut illa, inquam genuina debitaque Evangelii praedicatio, deinceps Dei, ut dictum est nomine ab illis, sive conscie sive inscie, continuaretur verbo non ὅλως insitè indubie mereque vero, id est non omnino insite ut διαφθορᾷ, ὀρεῖ, ἀχαλαγαστῳ, non in aeternum manente, & de quo toto quantum est, indubie verèque dici non potest, verbum tuum est veritas; videlicet quod nec ὅλως insitè indubie mereque verum est; nec de quo tum ipsimet illi continuatores, tum ii qui continuatorum istorum illos qui Ecclesiarum ministri sunt pro Dei ut dictum est nomine Evangelii, Zanetibus ministris, eorum autem alios illos qui Ecclesiarum ministri non sunt, pro genuinis caeteroquin Dei ut dictum illum Istum est nomine continuatoribus jam receperunt; de quo in- quam utrique tamen fiquam maxime velint & contendunt, per- inde ac de ipsissimo Dei verbo ὁ λόγος infitè indubiè mereq; ve- ro ἀψεύδης nec perfinet sunt nec esse possunt. Item, utrum De- us nomine ut dictum est sive ullam Evangelii praedicationem à ministris speciatim ac debitè ad eam missis datis & vocatis primitus inchoari & continuari voluerit, instituerit, man- dauerit, aut beneplacite permiserit, quae Dei nomine, seu Dei ut dictum est loca & authoritate, sive consiliè, sive insciè ab iis aliisve peragerentur verbo itidem ut dictum est mea ὄλως infitè indubiè mereque vero?
units.tr: 2. The author sets out his view of the apostate Church at pp. 26 to 32, repeats it at pp. 38 and 55, and in those passages chiefly lays down two formal grounds and charges of apostasy. I. The divine and infallible Word of God, the Word of God of the Old and New Testaments, which in the assemblies and public worship of the churches ought to be heard alone, is instead explained, handled and preached by the words of men who are not infallible and are not equally divine and infallible as the word of Holy Scripture. II. Yet that word of the assemblies is said to have God's name and authority, and so, as a third point, note what follows from it, according to question 165: it is handled not by everyone and anyone indiscriminately, but by certain ministers called and instructed for this purpose in the Church. The whole controversy he raises against us hangs on these two points, and the whole weight of his opinion rests on them. On these grounds he attacks the churches, not only ours but all who bear the Christian name, that is, all that have existed in the world from the beginning until now, from the times of the Apostles. On these grounds he accuses and condemns them, and in his eyes they appear as the mystery of iniquity, apostasy, false worship and everything antichristian. How he storms, cries out, warns and threatens, and how he shows that one must stand firm and that the earth shakes under such men! Question 22: We must ask whether those who, without any command, institution or permission of God in Holy Scripture on this matter, nevertheless continue in the name of God, that is, in God's place and authority, or as those who act as God's ambassadors, consciously or unconsciously, the twofold and due preaching of the Gospel, which was first begun and instituted by that word which is wholly, indubitably and purely true, as has been said, by the name of God, and carry on, institute and complete any preaching of the Gospel in the same way, in the name of God and as God's ambassadors, consciously or unconsciously, with the word, as has been said, which is not wholly, indubitably and purely true; I ask, whether they, by this very act, administer the same preaching of the Gospel as God wills it to be administered in his name, or whether they administer it by this very act as seems good to them and as they themselves wish? With what bombast of words, with what empty circling, periphrasis and repetition do you dispatch a matter of nothing, which could be settled easily and in a word? In other words, with great effort you produce great trifles. You want this to be asked: whether those who continue the preaching of the Gospel in God's name nevertheless administer that preaching, in a word and sermon not wholly and so infallibly as the Gospel itself, as he teaches, or as God wishes it to be exercised? Why so many words, idle epithets, repetitions of "likewise", and why so tortuously stated a controversy? Once you have explained what infallible word you demand in public sermons, which you call wholly, indubitably and purely true, why is the same thing repeated to nausea and to the distraction of the reader's attention in every paragraph? Once you have expounded what you think is to be understood by the name of God, which ought to be set forth, why does it return so often and so uselessly: "in the name of God, that is, in God's place and authority, or as for God", and so on? And on these two points, as is clear from this and other questions, the whole truth of the controversy turns: the infallible Word of God, and the holding of the name of God. Therefore. III. Chapter 4, question 1. He calls the churches imperfect because the former does not continue in the churches by men; and because they nevertheless have some sort of name of God and hold sermons, he calls them presumptuous. These two things seem to give rise to the apostasy of all Christian churches, for the case is similar for all of them. In question or article 18, page 25, in the Admonition, he states the true state of the controversy most clearly: Let us see, then. He speaks thus in the same place: First, it must be asked whether God, in Holy Scripture, has commanded or graciously permitted to some ministers of his Church, or to others, that the genuine and due preaching of the Gospel, which was first begun and instituted by God in the name of God, that is, in the place and authority of God, or as an ambassador for God (as has been said), should be carried on, by the word of Christ's promise, wholly, indubitably and purely true, entirely and in such a way as incorruptible, enduring, unchangeable and eternal, and of which the whole, as much as it was, could indubitably and truly be said, "Your word is truth"; that is, which was wholly, indubitably and purely true, and of which both those who preached it and those who had already received it, as has been said, could be and were persuaded, just as of God's very own word, wholly, indubitably and purely true, and without falsehood. Thus, I say, that genuine and due preaching of the Gospel was afterwards continued in God's name, as has been said, by those men, whether knowingly or unknowingly, with a word that is not wholly, indubitably and purely true, that is, not entirely such as is incorruptible, enduring and unchangeable, and of which the whole cannot be indubitably and truly said, "Your word is truth"; namely, that is not wholly, indubitably and purely true; and of which neither those continuers themselves, nor those who, of those continuers, are ministers of the churches, nor others who are not ministers of the churches, have received, for the name of God, as has been said, the Gospel for the sake of... (passage here is corrupt). Of which, I say, both parties, though they most strongly wish and contend, are not and cannot be sure, just as of God's own word, the Word, wholly, indubitably and purely true, and without falsehood. Also, whether God, in the name as has been said, has willed, instituted, commanded or graciously permitted any preaching of the Gospel to be first begun and continued by ministers specially and duly sent and called for this purpose, which in God's name, or in the place and authority of God as has been said, is carried on by them or others, consciously or unconsciously, with the word, likewise as has been said, not wholly, indubitably and purely true?

units.la: Non annotabo, quae semel iterumque ad inanem il- lam verbi infallibilis descriptionem, aut quid nomine Dei designetur, explicationem dixi, ne ejus in hac re fere similis evadam. Putasne ad accuratam disputandi methodum ac leges, Controversiae statum luculenter satis hic propositum? & breviter, nervosè, ac distinctè? nae si ita exis[?]s, graviter, meo quidem judicio, erras. Nam pri[?]s, quid sibi vult quod toties & tam emphaticè distingui vis, beneplacita Dei permissio? ut, quando quaeris, utrum Deus voluerit, instituerit, mandarit, aut beneplacitè permiserit? Quam intelligis Dei permissionem? & quomodo illam appellas beneplacitam, quam contradistinguis, & contrapponis ejus voluntati? expedi quid illa, verbo illo Christi promisso: quod promissum verbum putas? an Christum promisisse omnibus suis ministris etiam post Apostolos verbum λόγος divinum infallibile, quod, neque aliud continuò praedicarent? proba: & per illas futiles epexegeses verbi infitè, indubiè, &c. & quae longâ serie ibidem sequuntur, aliudne vis, quam quod nos dicimus, verbum infallibile? saltem illud peto, ut si haec nostra notio tibi minus placeat, aliam commodiorem, & significantiorem meâ istâ, & tuâ quoque tam prolixâ, periphrasi substituas, quae brevius sc. & expeditius inter disputandum teneatur: nemo enim est, quem non illa tam crebra & fastidiosa eorundem verborum repetitio offendat. Quale etiam illud est, in quo non minus per totum scriptum βαρβαλογίας, sive conscie, sive inscie, an ab aliquibus Dei nomine continuari Euangelii præ[…] predicatio possit verbo non ἀλλ’ s, &c. divino, inscie? illud tamen hic dicis isto tuo siue conscie, siue inscie: atque sic sæpius parum consideraté. Quidquid sit, ingenuè judica, annoa commodiùs & distinctiùs controversia hoc articulo indicata sic proponatur: An Deus mandarit, vel permiserit, aut concesserit verbum suum in Ecclesiis prædicari, nomine etiam suo, à Præconibus non-infallibilibus? vel annota, quæ in constituendo Controversiæ statu à me sic forte neglecta sint. Et hæc est Apostatica tua Ecclesia, vel potiùs apostaticus Christianismus: quia non de aliquâ inter Christianos Ecclesiâ sic sentis, sed de universo & Catholico Christianismo.
units.tr: I shall not note how often I have said that the empty description of the word "infallible", or the explanation of what "in the name of God" designates, is not an explanation, lest I become like you in this matter. Do you think that the state of the controversy is set out here clearly enough for an accurate method and rules of disputation, and briefly, forcefully and distinctly? Indeed, if you think so, you are, in my judgment, gravely mistaken. For first, what do you mean by the distinction you so often and so emphatically want made, "the gracious permission of God"? When you ask whether God has willed, instituted, commanded, or graciously permitted, what do you understand by God's "permission"? And how do you call it "gracious", which you set apart from and oppose to his "will"? Explain what you mean by "that word of Christ's promise". What promised word do you have in mind? Do you mean that Christ promised all his ministers, even after the Apostles, a divine and infallible word, which they would not preach as something else? Prove it. And through those empty explanations of "the word wholly, indubitably," and so on, and what follows in the long series there, do you mean anything other than what we call an "infallible" word? At least I ask this: if this notion of ours displeases you, substitute another more convenient and more meaningful than mine, and no less prolix than yours, one that can be kept briefer and more readily in disputation. For no one is not offended by that tiresome and frequent repetition of the same words. Such is also that in which, throughout the whole writing, no less [...] "whether by some, consciously or unconsciously, the preaching of the Gospel can be carried on in God's name with a word not wholly divine" [...] unconsciously? Yet here you say "consciously or unconsciously", and so often rather carelessly. Whatever the case, judge frankly: would it not be better and clearer if the controversy indicated in this article were put thus: "Has God commanded, permitted or granted that his word be preached in the churches, in his own name too, by preachers who are not infallible?" Or note what, in setting up the state of the controversy, I may perhaps have neglected. And this is your "apostate" Church, or rather apostate Christianity, because you judge not of some one church among Christians, but of all Christianity, universal and catholic.

units.la: Post Apostolicam, & Apostaticam, sequitur Ecclesiam observemus Connivenìq quam appellas. Vbi tria attendo. 1. quomodo omnes Christianismi Ecclesias, propter apostasiam illam scilicet, quâ de jam diximus, etiam nostras Reformatas fastuosè condemnas, quum ipse interim, quod perquam ridiculum & intolerandum, reprehendas, quod inter Christianos Ecclesiæ aliæ alias condemnant: & tu verò, quo jure omnes? 11. deseris Ecclesiam, & ab illâ secedis tu,atque aliis idem imperas, si quidem saluti & pietati consultum velint. Sicque schisma, ut à cœtibus malignantium scilicet, moliris. 111. quomodo tuam aliam Connivenciæ erigas, atque in illam transcundum existimes, ultimò videbimus. In quibus, ut hoc obiter addam, turpiter tuis aliis hypothesibus es contrarius: putas enim inter omnes, quotquot sub nomine Christiano diversæ sunt ac scissæ, Ecclesias vel sectas, syncretismum coli debere, ac convenicndum omnibus esse inter se-colendamque unionem, quia non adeo à se dissentiunt & pugnant in fundamentalibus salutis; interim oomnes Christianismi Ecclesias jam non uniendas, sed dese-rendas, ac de novo scindi, quasi non schismatum satis foret, aliamque sectam contra omnium Ecclesiarum coitionem, doces.
units.tr: After Apostolicam and Apostaticam, let us observe what follows, the Connivence that you call it. Here I note three things. First, how you scornfully condemn all the Churches of Christendom, our Reformed Churches included, on account of that apostasy which I have already mentioned. Yet at the same time you rebuke, in a manner that is most ridiculous and intolerable, the fact that Christian churches condemn one another. By what right do you condemn them all? Second, you urge people to desert the Church and withdraw from it, and you command others to do the same, if they wish to look to their salvation and piety. In this way you plan a schism, as if from the assemblies of the wicked. Third, we shall see at the end how you set up your other Connivence and think that people should pass over into it. In these matters, to add this in passing, you are shamefully at odds with your other hypotheses. For you think that all who bear the Christian name but are divided and split into different churches or sects should practise a syncretism, that they should come together and that unity should be cultivated among them, because they do not differ and fight so much over the fundamentals of salvation. Yet you teach that all the Churches of Christendom should not now be united but deserted, and split afresh, as if there were not enough schisms already, and as if a new sect should be set up against the union of all the Churches.

units.la: Quomodo vero, quod primo nobis perpendendum omnes totius Christianismi Ecclesias, earumque ministerium, conciones, confessiones, catecheses, preces, cantiones, disciplinam, Synodos, & quod ridiculum, acta classicalia, consistorialia, scholas, promotionem & gradus scholasticos, &c. condemnes, videre licet ab erot. Lxv. & deinceps, sive à pag. 39. ubi quæris, quonam igitur modo verbum illud ab avo hodieque ministrorum concionatorium, &c. tolli possit? atque iterum pag. 46. vel erot. xci. nam eò usque strenuè nugaris de S. Scripturæ insufficientiâ, obscuritate, & latitudine: breviter enim respondere licet, neque verbum Dei aut S. Scripturam insufficientem esse. nec conciones ideo nostras tollendas; quia ut verbum concionatorium, quod appellas, non substituitur à nobis loco S. Scripturæ, nedum ut præferatur; ita illa duo invicem non pugnant, ut habeatur Scriptura S. sufficientissima, & interim ex eâ conciones, quo illa reddatur nobis, cui usui revera data est, ὠφέλιμος πρὸς διδασκαλίαν, πρὸς ἔλεγχον &c. II Tim. III. 16. Hic enim est perpetuus tuus paralogismus, quod opponas ut contraria verbum Dei, & S. conciones; quum opponenda non sint, sed conjungenda & subordinanda, puta conciones verbo divino; adeóque peccas, quod Logici dicunt, fallacia oppositionis. Porrò, non alium vis Catechismum, & Confessionem, quam nudum Dei verbum, idcoque catechismos & confessiones superciliosè respuis, erot. xcIv. &c. quod ex eodem errore profluit, quasi catechismus, & confessio, præsupposito quod vera sint (nam secus nemo pro illis disputaverit, & tu te hic frustra opposueris,) cum illo Dei verbo nequeant consistere, eique necessario adversentur: & hinc, mirum quàm imprudenter, addo & impudenter,erotem. xcv i i. Ecclesiæ affingis, quod Catechismum, & Confessionem, ut aliud Dei verbum, præ vel juxta S. Scripturam, adhibeat; quod notorie falsum est. Quid vero cantus, quid preces, quid administrationis sacramentorum, baptismi, cœnæque formulæ; quid ministrorum, seniorum, Diaconorum ordinationes, & functiones; quid acta consistorialia, classica- lia, synodalia; quid formulæ matrimonii confirmandi, & disciplinæ in Ecclesiâ exercendæ: quid consolatorias ægrotorum, vel publica jejunia; quid denique S. Scripturæ versiones, commentarii, conciones, loci communes, thesfes, (rissum quæso teneatis) scholæ itidem & Academia, vocationes Doctoratus, Professoratus, librorum censura. Publici scripturæ anagnostæ, prælectores, aliaque quæ vel ad regimen Ecclesiæ, aut scholarum spectant, quod ista omnia unâ litura levissimè deles, atque condemnas? erot. cxlviii. cxii. & seq. quid, inquam, illa commiserunt, quidve in illis tam grave piaculum, quod non aliter quam universali eorundem ablatione & diluvio corrigendum existimes? vel, meliusne tum fore arbitraris in Ecclesiâ, sume etiam tuâ illâ aliâ, hæc ubi non habueris? si respondeas, te non simpliciter illa aversari; sed ut apud nos ea exerceri videntur, Dei nomine: regero, probes primùm illa omnia æquè apud nos ut Dei nomine administrari, vel haberi. Tum distinctius explica, quid Dei nomine intelligas, & an putes omnia, eorumque usum, prout in Ecclesiis nostris habentur, prorsus destitui Dei jussu, vel authoritate, explicitè vel implicitè, universalius vel singularius illa mandante aut approbante? vel ad tuam distinctionem erot. cxxxiv. loquendo, hæc ex S.S. literis non aliquatenus colligi posse. neque enim puto quempiam tam miseri sincipitis, qui tuâ vanâ jactantiâ, temerè omnia etiam minutissima quæque in Ecclesiis sive scholis nostris respuente & concuIcante moveatur, ob simplicem, ne dicam, stultam sententiam, aut erotematicam propositionem: Ne-
units.tr: Next, what we must first weigh: you condemn all the Churches of the whole of Christendom, and their ministry, sermons, confessions, catechisms, prayers, hymns, discipline, synods and, what is ridiculous, the acts of classes and consistories, schools, promotion and scholastic degrees, and so on. This can be seen from erot. 65 onwards, or from pag. 39, where you ask how that word of the ministers' preaching, handed down from grandfather even to today, etc., could be removed? and again at pag. 46, or erot. 91. For you trifle at length there about the insufficiency, obscurity and breadth of Holy Scripture. Briefly, one may answer that neither the Word of God nor Holy Scripture is insufficient, nor should our sermons therefore be abolished. For the preaching, which you call the word of preaching, is not substituted by us in place of Holy Scripture, much less preferred to it. Nor do these two things fight against each other, so that Holy Scripture may be held to be most sufficient and yet sermons be drawn from it, by which it is made available to us, for which purpose it was indeed given: profitable for teaching, for reproof, etc. (2 Tim. 3:16) [ὠφέλιμος πρὸς διδασκαλίαν, πρὸς ἔλεγχον]. For this is your constant paralogism, that you set the Word of God and Holy sermons against each other as if they were contraries, whereas they are not to be opposed but joined and subordinated, namely sermons to the divine Word. So you commit what the logicians call the fallacy of opposition. Further, you want no catechism or confession but the bare Word of God, and so you scornfully reject catechisms and confessions, erot. 94 and so on. This arises from the same error, as if a catechism and a confession, presupposing that they are true (for otherwise no one would argue for them, and you would be wasting your effort here), could not stand with that Word of God and must necessarily oppose it. Hence, and it is astonishing how imprudently, I add, and how impudently, you charge the Church in erot. 97 with using the catechism and confession as though they were another Word of God, either above or alongside Holy Scripture, which is notoriously false. But what about the songs, what about the prayers, what about the formulas for administering the sacraments, baptism and the Supper; what about the ordinations and functions of ministers, elders and deacons; what about the acts of consistories, classes and synods; what about the formulas of marriage, of confirmation, and of the discipline to be exercised in the Church; what about the comforting of the sick or public fasts; and finally, what about the translations of Holy Scripture, commentaries, sermons, commonplaces, theses (I beg you keep your laughter in check), schools likewise and universities, the calling to doctorates and professorships, and the censorship of books. What about the public readers and lecturers of Scripture, and the other things that concern the government of the Church or of the schools? Do you condemn and cancel all these with a single stroke, most lightly? See erot. 148, 112 and following. What, I ask, have they done, or what is so grave a crime in them that you think it must be corrected by the universal removal and deluge of all of them? Or do you think that things would be better in the Church, even in your other one, where you would have none of these? If you answer that you do not reject them outright, but only as they seem to be practised among us in God's name, I reply: first prove that all these things are administered or held among us in God's name alike. Then explain more distinctly what you mean by in God's name, and whether you think that all of them, and their use, as they are held in our Churches, are wholly lacking in God's command or authority, explicitly or implicitly, more generally or more particularly commanding or approving them. Or, speaking in your own distinction (erot. 134), do you say that these things cannot be gathered in any way from the Holy Scriptures? For I do not think there is anyone of such a wretched head that, under your vain boasting, he would be rashly moved, by a simple, not to say foolish, opinion or an erotematic proposition, to reject and shake off even the smallest things in our Churches or schools. [Latin continues in the next unit.]

units.la: Neque etiam à tuo illo, quem frequentas, & ducis, coetu, omnia quae te audivimus in Ecclesiis nostris indignè contemnere, absunt: ut quae de verbi publicâ lectione, explicatione, concione, consolatione, & precibus dixisti, illa non omnino à vobis negliguntur: quare particulatim magis explicandum fuerat, quâ ratione illa apud nos non castigata, sed omnino abolita ac remota velis. Caeterum te ipsum interroga, tuamque conscientiam, fructus studiorum tuorum tibi memorantem: jam credere nequeo te serio arbitrari scholas omnes studiaque scholastica vel in genere, vel nostra simpliciter & absolutè proscribi posse. Et puto, vel hoc unum sufficere satis posse contra sententiam tuam; estque absurdissimum, quod ex eâ statuis, abstinere nos debere à concionibus, à Catechismis & confessionibus nostris, λωγς insitè indubiè merèque veris, Dei ut dictum est nomine condendis, & usurpandis adhibendis; à sacramentis Dei ut dictum est nomine administrandis; à supercilio, & aliarum Ecclesiarum pro se contemtu & excommunicatione, à vocandis ordinandis & mittendis Dei nomine ministris, item à fidei inquisitione, à regimine Ecclesiae, disciplinâque Ecclesiasticâ eo quo faciunt modo, Dei ut dictum est nomine exercenda; à liturgiis aliisque consistorialibus, classicalibus, ac synodalibus, statutisque caeteroquin Ecclesiasticis, ut faciunt Dei nomine, seu tanquam pro Deo legatione fungendo, condendis, promulgandis, & injungendis; à petendo ut vocant, brachio saeculari ad haereticos quos vocant, & schismaticos puniendos; à publicis populi, nomine Dei, benedictionibus; à publicis precibus pro universo populo, tanquam à ministris, qui legatione pro Christo fungantur, ad Deum habitis; ab hymnis itidem condendis, qui publicè tanquam genuini divini cultus pars à populo in Ecclesiâ canentur; à formulis administrationis baptismi & caenae Dominicae; ordinationis ministrorum, seniorum Ecclesiae, & Diaconorum; à formulis matrimoniorum, excommunicationis, receptionis, & admissionis in Ecclesiam; depositionis ministrorum, conSolatoriis ægrotantium; privatarum precum; à formulis indictionis jejuniorum publicorum, & dierum publicis precibus destinandorum; à formulis ordinandorum in Ecclesiâ festorum, rituum, & ceremoniarum; quæ scilicet omnes formulæ, tanquam à ministris nomine Dei legatione fungentibus fabricatæ fuerint: adhæc à S. Scripturæ versionibus; scriptis commentariis; scriptis concionibus, locis communibus, thesibus, aliisque similibus, tanquam à ministris, qui Dei nomine legationem obeant, factis & populo exhibitis: à scholis itidem & Academiis, quas vocant aperiendis, erigendis, & regendis; à Doctoratus, Baccalaureatus, Professoratus Theologiæ, ut loquuntur, vocationibus, electionibus, confirmationibus & ordinationibus: à librorum censurâ, & permissione & prohibitione impressionis Typographicæ; publicorum sacræ Scripturæ anagnostarum, prædicatorum, & consolatorum ordinatione; & conversationis cum aliorum cœtuum Christianis prohibitione: à prohibitione publicæ mutuæ Christianorum ædificationis; à publicâ fidei professione à Christianis deponenda, & ratione convertendi errantes & ignorantes præscribenda: item & cæteris omnibus, quæ in munniis Ecclesiasticis, vel sine prævia debitâ vocatione & missione, ad ea prædictorumque munera Dei nomine seu pro Deo legatione fungendo peragenda, vel en in Dei ut dictum est tolerantia & conniveнтia, sine accurata illa S. Scripturæ indagine ac directione, fieri, Ecclesiastica authoritate, nomine membrorum Ecclesiæ respectivorum, & jure communi vocationis, non debent? sic enim paratrægadiatis, erot. cxlviii. Quid, etiam à ratione convertendi errantes & ignorantes, jubes nos cavere? quod ego quidem & omnes mecum pii, quibus ἀλας non omnino ἀνάλον, Marc. ix. 50. vel ut Plautus loquitur in Pœnulo, qui non ἀλα ἀγρα ἀμῶ, impiissimum pronunciabunt, & prodiudiosæ sententiæ certissimum argumentum. Et, à publicâ fidei professione à Christianis deponendâ nos quoque arces: aut nihil ego video; aut hæc compendiosissima est ad infidelitatem atque ad Atheismum via. De conse-quenquentia mea, vel potius tuo illo antecedenti volo omnes judicent: nondum enim ex professo argumentis contra te ago; & dispiciant, an tion ejusmodi in negotio religionis & Christianâ statuere, satis sit ad explodendam sententiam, eamque cum Auctore suo rejiciendam?
units.tr: Nor are you absent from that assembly which you frequent and lead, in which, as we have heard, you unworthily despise everything in our Churches. For what you said about the public reading of the Word, its explanation, preaching, comfort and prayers is not wholly neglected by us. Therefore it should have been explained item by item in what way you want those things to be removed from us, not merely corrected but utterly abolished. Otherwise, question yourself and your conscience, which recalls to you the fruits of your studies. I cannot believe that you seriously think that all schools and scholastic studies can be banned, either in general or our own simply and absolutely. And I think this one point alone is enough to refute your opinion, and it is most absurd that, from your view, we ought to abstain from sermons, from our catechisms and confessions, framed in God's name, by reasons implanted in us, indubitably and purely true [λόγοις]; from administering the sacraments in God's name; from the arrogance and contempt of other Churches and their excommunication; from calling, ordaining and sending ministers in God's name; likewise from the inquiry into faith, from the government of the Church, and from ecclesiastical discipline, which are exercised in God's name in the way they do; from composing and promulgating and imposing liturgies and other consistorial, classical and synodal matters and statutes, which are otherwise ecclesiastical, as they do in God's name, or as performing an embassy on behalf of God; from asking, as they call it, the secular arm to punish those they call heretics and schismatics; from public blessings of the people in God's name; from public prayers for the whole people, held before God by ministers who discharge an embassy for Christ; likewise from composing hymns which are sung publicly in the Church by the people as a genuine part of divine worship; from formulas for administering baptism and the Lord's Supper; from the ordination of ministers, elders and deacons; from formulas for marriages, excommunication, reception and admission into the Church, the deposition of ministers, comfort for the sick, private prayers; from formulas for announcing public fasts and days appointed for public prayers; from formulas for festivals, rites and ceremonies to be observed in the Church. All these formulas, namely, must be regarded as made by ministers who discharge an embassy in God's name. Besides, from translations of Holy Scripture; from written commentaries; from written sermons, commonplaces, theses and other similar things, made and presented to the people as by ministers who undertake an embassy in God's name; likewise from opening, founding and governing schools and universities, as they call them; from the calling, electing, confirming and ordaining of doctors, bachelors and professors of theology, as they speak; from censoring books, and from permitting and forbidding printing; from the ordaining of public readers, preachers and comforters of Scripture; and from the prohibition of fellowship with Christians of other assemblies; from the prohibition of public mutual edification among Christians; from the requirement that Christians lay aside public profession of faith, and that a method of converting the erring and ignorant be prescribed; likewise from all the other things which in ecclesiastical offices, without prior due calling and sending, or which are done in God's name or as an embassy on behalf of God, or which are done by the tolerance and connivance of God, as you put it, without that careful inquiry and direction of Holy Scripture, by ecclesiastical authority, in the name of the respective members of the Church and by the common right of calling, ought not to be done? For so you lay out your case, erot. 148. What is more, you bid us beware of the method of converting the erring and ignorant. This indeed I and all the godly with me, for whom the salt has not become altogether tasteless [ἅλας μὴ ἄναλον, Mark 9:50], will pronounce most impious, and a most certain proof of a headstrong opinion. And you also warn us against requiring Christians to lay aside public profession of faith. Either I see nothing, or this is the shortest road to unbelief and atheism. On my consequence, or rather on your antecedent, I want everyone to judge. For I have not yet argued against you in form; let them consider whether, in a matter of religion and Christian faith, it is enough to set up such a view in order to explode the opinion and reject it together with its author?

units.la: Hactenus Ecclesiam nostram, omniaque nostra satis confidenter condemnasti; & hinc eodem pergis pede ac audaciâ, eam ut pestiferam, schisma ab eâ, & defectionem palàm suadendo, quod secundò nobis advertendum proposuimus. Concedis tamen licitè communicare cum eâ, quantoperè defectivâ, quamdiu sine ignorantiâ peccavit, erot. clv i rr. At vero, quando jam meliora à te edocta, de erigendâ puta Ecclesiâ tuâ connivetiæ, & hoc insuper habens non curat, atque intrepidè suo antiquo more pergit, jam tibi ne quidem Ecclesia ulterius appellanda videtur: si ejusmodi ἀνθρωποι cœtus nihilominus neque cultum suum priorem desinant: neque connivetia (ut dictum est) cultum instituant; Tum inquam querendum est, utrum homini Christiano à talibus cœtibus, cuilibet à suo, se tunc separare omnino necesse sit, habendo cœtus illos non amplius nomine Ecclesiæ Dei; sed cœtuum malignantium, in quos homines Deum timentis, ejusque ἀλως; insiste indubiè mereque verum scriptum verbum unicè sequentis, anima intrare non debeat? bona verba quaeso. ad quam quaestionem sic tutè respondes, ut non tam de affirmativa ponenda, nedum probanda solicitus videaris; sed ea tacitè omissa, attamen concessa, statim in modum inquiras, quo illa secessio ab Ecclesiâ instituenda sit, publicène an privatim, &c. erot. clxv i. tum querendum est, quomodo homo Christianus se quoad religiosi cultus exercitium gerere debeat, postquam cœtum illum vanum debitè reliquit. Et primò quidem privatum à secessione cultum sequi jubes, qui veri publici scilicet cultus vices tuo judicio supplet, erot. clxx. Tum etiam publicum cœtum ac cultum vis erigi, erot. clxxiv. puta istum Connivëntia; de quo nos tertiò, postquam intellexerimus ut Ecclesias omnes condemnes, etiamdeferas, loquendum duximus, qualem tuum coetum mediteris, quidve in eo agi velis.
units.tr: Until now you have condemned our Church and all that is ours quite confidently, and from there you press on with the same boldness, urging that it be regarded as pestilential and that people separate from it and openly break away, which is the second point we proposed to address. Yet you concede that one may lawfully communicate with it, however defective, as long as it sins without knowledge (erot. clvii). But when it has been taught better things and still does not care to set up your church of connivance, and moreover, keeping this in view, goes on fearlessly in its old manner, you think it should no longer even be called a Church. If such assemblies of men [ἀνθρωποι] neither abandon their former worship nor institute worship under connivance (as has been said), then I ask: must a Christian man altogether separate himself from such assemblies, each from his own, on the ground that they are no longer to be counted as Churches of God but as assemblies of malignants, into which a man who fears God and his [ὅλως] ought not to enter, if he follows the written word alone, undoubtedly and purely? Good words, I beg you. To this question you answer so cautiously that you seem anxious not so much to lay down the affirmative, let alone prove it, but, leaving it tacitly omitted yet granted, you at once ask in what manner that secession from the Church is to be carried out, publicly or privately, etc. (erot. clxv). Then it must be asked how a Christian man should conduct himself in the exercise of religious worship after he has duly left that empty assembly. First, you bid him follow private worship apart from secession, which, in your judgment, supplies the place of true public worship (erot. clxx). Then you also want a public assembly and worship set up (erot. clxxiv). Let us call that one Connivance; concerning which we have thought it necessary to speak in the third place, after we have understood that you condemn all churches, even dismissing them, namely, what kind of assembly you are planning and what you wish to be done in it.

units.la: Appellas coetum Connivëntiæ, dignâ hypothesi nomenclaturâ, quia nimirum ob diuturnam omnium totius Christianismi Ecclesiarum apostasiam offenso Deo, sub ejus irâ, vel indulgentiâ, in Dei displicitâ tolerantiâ, hoc defectivo Ecclesiæ statu, ut loqui amas, colligitur. Agit de hâc suâ Ecclesiâ Auctor à pag. 57. vel erot. cxxviii. & dein ceps. Quaerendum est, Virum Deus in SS. literis instituerit, mandarit, vel beneplacitè permiserit, ut talis defectiva Ecclesia, Ecclesias in Dei displiciti tolerantia, condad populi sui jam dictos defectus aliósque conniveнтia, erigeret, colligeret & regeret: non quidem Dei nomine, seu pro Deo legatione fungendo; sed Dei quidem previa ad id ut dictum est connivëntia, & quam proximè fieri potest ὅλως insitè indubiè merèque verè cum ὅλως insitè indubiè merèque veris: attamen authoritate duntaxat talis Christianismi Ecclesiastica, nomine membrorum talis Ecclesiæ respectivorum, sed tanquam membra talis Ecclesiæ respectiva, & jure vocationis talium Christianorum communi: ita ut error ibi tolerari possit ac debeat? & erot. cxxxiv. limitatius idem quaerit, non an probari possit ex Dei instituto vel beneplacitâ permissione; sed an alio quovis pacto, ex S. literis illud possit colligi? Tum quaerendum est; Virum in S.S. literis loca habeantur (in quibus non quidem instituatur, mandetur aut beneplacitè permittatur, sed) unde aliquatenus colligi possit à Deo tolerari, quod jam dicto Ecclesiæ statu defectivo Ecclesiæ in Dei displiciti tolerantia; erigantur: ubi quaeso nota distinctionem, quam facit, inter Dei beneplacitam permissionem; & tolerantiam, quorum membrorum oppositionem volo primum nobis demonstret, maximè quum primum istorum quod aliàs etiam adhibere solet omittat, nim. an Deus voluerit &c. & quomodo haec membra distincta sint, explicet.
