Interim contra ejus erotema aliud pono: Vtrum talis distinctio inter Dei voluntatem, mandatum, beneplacitam permissionem, atque tolerantiam ex S. S. literis probari possit? sed ad erotemata ipsa. Si ubi in hoc defectivo, ex tua mente, Ecclesiarum statu ecclesiae eriguntur, in Dei displicith tolerantiâ, & ad populi sui jam dictos defectus aliosque connivetiâ; ergo, etiamnum connivet Deus nobis, nostrisque defectibus: quare tu ergo ob illos nos condemnas, & deserendos nostros coetus, ut malignantium, in quos hominis Deum timentis anima intrare non debeat, existimas? erot. clxii. ii.
units.tr: You call the assembly a Connivance-assembly, a fitting name for the hypothesis, because, namely, on account of the long-standing apostasy of all the Churches of Christendom, God being offended, it is gathered under his wrath or indulgence, in a toleration displeasing to God, in this defective state of the Church, as you love to put it. The author treats of this his Church from page 57 or erot. cxxviii and onward. It must be asked whether God in the Holy Scriptures has instituted, commanded, or graciously permitted that such a defective Church, in a toleration displeasing to God, under connivance at the defects of his people and others already mentioned, should be erected, gathered, and governed; not indeed in God's name, or by serving as God's ambassador, but by the previous connivance of God, as has been said, and as nearly as possible wholly [ὅλως], undoubtedly and purely with the wholly, undoubtedly and purely true; yet only by the authority of such a Christian ecclesiastical body, in the name of the respective members of such a Church, but as the respective members of such a Church, and by the right of the common calling of such Christians; so that error may be and ought to be tolerated there? (erot. cxxxiv). He asks the same more narrowly: not whether it can be proved from God's institution or gracious permission, but whether it can be gathered from the Scriptures in any other way. Then it must be asked whether in the Holy Scriptures there are passages (in which it is not instituted, commanded, or graciously permitted, but) from which it can be somewhat gathered that God tolerates, in a toleration displeasing to God, that such a defective Church should be erected in the said defective state of the Church; where I ask you to note the distinction he makes between God's gracious permission and toleration, the opposition of which members I want him first to demonstrate to us, especially since he omits the first of these, which he is otherwise accustomed to use, namely whether God has willed etc., and he explains how these members are distinct. Meanwhile I set against his question another: whether such a distinction between God's will, command, gracious permission and toleration can be proved from the Holy Scriptures? But to the questions themselves. If, in your mind, in this defective state of the Churches, churches are erected in a toleration displeasing to God, and under connivance at the defects of his people already mentioned and others, then God still connives at us and our defects. Why, then, do you condemn us on account of those defects, and judge our assemblies to be those of malignants into which the soul of a man who fears God ought not to enter? (erot. clxii).

units.la: Ergo adhuc Deo sumus ejus populus, dum nobis connivet, ut ad populi sui defectus aquare itaque tibi ne nomine quidem Ecclesiae digni videntur? erot. clxiii. iii. Ergo nec tua jam Ecclesia, quam meditaris, vera vel optima est, sed & defectiva etiam, neque cum Dei approbatione, vel ejus mandato; sed sub ejus connivenția, indignatione, atque tolerantiâ colligitur, erroresque tolerare adhucdum debet. In quo hoc unum nobis gratulor, quod ita te conscientia hoc in negotio pupugerit, ut non aliter tuam Ecclesiam commendare potueris, quam vitiosam: (quae quorsum adametur, vel etiam quomodo adiri à sanis, cum nostra commutata possit, ego non video. iv. Dicis, Ecclesiam tuam erigi non Dei nomine, &c. jure ergo meritoque ei regerimus: si non sit ex coelo, sed ex hominibus, neque necesse est ei assentiri. Luc. xx. 4, 5. v. Proba, illam Connivetiae ecclesiam erigi, & sistendam sub Dei connivetiâ, & non sub ejus irâ & indignatione, juxta cum aliis Ecclesiis; vel Deum tuis connivere potius, quam irasci. Sim primum de eo certus. vi. Explica, quod de Ecclesiâ tuâ jactas, eam colligi quam proximè fieri potest ὁλως insitè indubiè mereque vere, cum ὁλως insitè indubiè mereque veris, nisi hoc sit ὁλως insitè indubiè mereque vere nugatum. Putas fortè tuam eccleclesiam proxime accedere ad infallibilem Apostolicam, ὁ λος mereque divinam: sed, praeterquam quod id non probes, neque n. tibi somnianti fidem nostram locavimus; etiam ipse evertis, dum errores ibi tolerari posse ac debere asseriss VII. Quomodo dicis tuam ecclesiam colligi authoritate Christianismi Ecclesiastica, quum in Christianismo nullas veras Ecclesias; vel Ecclesiasticum regimen, vel authoritatem agnoscas? Deinde statim post dicis, Ecclesiam tuam erigi jure vocationis Christianorum & membrorum Ecclesiae communis. An tibi jam idem sunt, aliquid agere vocatione & authoritate vel nomine Ecclesiae, & nomine privato, ex communi omnium vocatione, ac officio? Sed, haec obiter tantum, & explorandae, discutiendae, examinandaeque sententiae gratia magis, quam impugnandae adhuc dicta; disputatio enim mox sequetur; sed in antecessum haec ad controversiam constituendam agitanda fuerunt, & secuturae argumentationi praestruenda; ut interim quoque perspiceretur argumentorum post adferendorum genuina ratio, ac scopus.
units.tr: Therefore we are still God's people, as long as he connives at us, so that we may be equal to the defects of his people; so that you do not think us worthy even of the name of Church? (erot. clxiii). Therefore neither is your Church, which you are planning, true or best, but defective also, and not with God's approval or by his command, but under his connivance, indignation, and toleration it is gathered, and it must still tolerate errors. In this one thing I congratulate us, that your conscience has so pricked you in this matter that you could not commend your Church otherwise than as faulty (what it is to be loved for, or how it can be approached by sane people, since ours can be changed, I do not see). iv. You say your Church is erected not in God's name, etc.; therefore we rightly and justly reject it: if it is not from heaven but from men, it is not necessary to assent to it (Luke 20:4, 5). v. Prove that that Connivance-church is erected and set up under God's connivance, and not under his wrath and indignation, just as the other Churches are; or else that God connives at your church rather than being angry. I would first be certain of that. vi. Explain what you boast of your Church, that it is gathered as nearly as possible wholly [ὅλως], undoubtedly and purely, with the wholly, undoubtedly and purely true, unless this is a wholly, undoubtedly and purely true trifling. Perhaps you think your church comes near to the infallible, apostolic, wholly and divine; but, apart from the fact that you do not prove it, we have not put our trust in your dreaming; you yourself overturn it, while you assert that errors can and ought to be tolerated there. vii. How do you say your church is gathered by the authority of the Christian ecclesiastical body, when you acknowledge in Christianity no true Churches, nor any ecclesiastical government or authority? Next, you immediately add that your Church is erected by the right of the calling of Christians and the common members of the Church. Are doing something by calling and authority, or in the name of the Church, and doing it in a private name, from the common calling and duty of all, the same thing to you? But these points are raised only in passing, and more for the sake of testing, discussing, and examining your opinion than for refuting what has been said; for the disputation will soon follow. Yet these matters had to be raised in advance, to set up the controversy and to lay the groundwork for the argument to come, so that meanwhile the genuine reason and aim of the arguments to be adduced afterwards might also be seen.

units.la: Futilissimum est, quod sequitur, erotema CXXIX. Si dicatur, quod Deus in S. S. literis instituerit, mandarit, vel beneplacite permiserit, oportet institutionem illam, mandata, vel beneplacitas permissiones proferre: ut de iis cogitetur. ecquid inanius? tuum erat proferre institutionem, mandata, vel beneplacitas permissiones, uti loqueris; non ab aliis illa exigere? siquidem de tua sententia hic agitur. Egone adigar, atque a te, tuam sententiam ut confirmem, & quidem locis Scripturae, quum illam quia ipse nullis probare potes, ideo & meritissimè rideam? Tuum est sollicitum esse, & sudare in perquirendis argumentis, σφρηνῆς Γυμναλείδη. Simile est erot. CXXXII. Sin autem responsum fuerit, quod defectivum dictum est Ecclesia statu, Ecclesia erigi, colligi & regi possint: Tum quaerendum est; quonam igitur modo id convenienter fieri possit? Hem quam callide! Scirmo est de probatione tuæ sententiæ vel Ecclesiæ: illam perridiculè poscis ab aliis, quam ipse debere præstare; neque allatâ eâ, statim prosilis ad modum, quo Ecclesiæ tales erigendæ sint. Profectò nimis ridicule. Erotemate cxxxv. dicis, Si dicatur, quod de Ecclesiastica illâ Ecclesiæ in Dei ut dictum est tolerantia, & conniventia erigendi colligendi, & regendi ratione nil in S. scriptura habeatur. Tum petendum est, ut qui id dicunt, S. S. literas prius accuratè ea de re consulant. tu Scripturas prius accuratè consulas, & tua si quæas, illic ostende: annon affirmantis est probare? nos negamus, & vel tuâ ipsius sententiâ, nescivit hactenus universus mundus talia, quæ tu jam de Ecclesiâ proponis, in Scripturis contineri; atque petis, ut nos illa in sacris reperiamus, monstremusque? nempe quia ipse id non potes.
units.tr: What follows, question 129, is most trifling. If it be said that God in the Holy Scriptures has instituted, commanded, or graciously permitted, it is necessary to produce that institution, those commands, or gracious permissions, so that people may think about them. What could be emptier? Was it not your task to produce the institution, commands, or gracious permissions, as you put it, rather than demanding them from others? For here it is your opinion that is at issue. Am I to be driven to confirm your opinion, and indeed by passages of Scripture, when I could rightly and most deservedly laugh at it, since you can prove it by no one? It is yours to be anxious and to sweat in seeking arguments, [σφρηνῆς Γυμναλείδη]. The same holds for erot. cxxxii. But if it is answered that, in the said defective state of the Church, churches can be erected, gathered, and governed, then it must be asked: in what way can this be done fittingly? Oh, how cunning! The proof of your opinion or of the Church is the business at hand; you most absurdly demand from others what you yourself ought to supply; and without producing it, you at once leap to the manner in which such churches are to be erected. Truly, too ridiculous. In question cxxxv you say: If it is said that nothing is to be found in Holy Scripture about the manner of erecting, gathering, and governing that ecclesiastical Church under God's toleration and connivance, as has been said, then it must be sought that those who say so first consult the Holy Scriptures carefully on that matter. Should you not first consult the Scriptures carefully yourself, and if you seek any, show them there? Is it not for the one who affirms to prove it? We deny it; and even by your own opinion, the whole world has hitherto not known that such things as you now propose concerning the Church are contained in the Scriptures; and you ask that we find and show them in the sacred books, precisely because you yourself cannot.

units.la: Erot. cxxxvi. Sin autem responsum fueris, esse tale loca in S. S. literis ad Ecclesias, &c. sic erigendas: Tum quætendum est; utrum loca illa S. scripturæ sint in suâ aliquâ ejus parte, an autem hinc inde per universum S. contextum sparsa? At jam responsum, loca in S. S. literis nullibi pro tuis illis Ecclesiis reperiri: quorsum ergo inoffenso & securo pede pergis, & quasi S. locorum copiâ laborares, ita illam formas quæstionem? Hic cogita, quod in Monito intempestivè dixisti, illud revera esse præpostero causæ præjudicio abreptum cum larvis suis, pro ordinis istius genio, luctari ac nugari, talia miselulis discipulis nimium credulis velle persuadere. agnoscis opinor tua. Erot. cxxxvii. Si dicatur, loca illa esse in suâ aliquâ S. scripturæ parte, oportet loca illa proferre. Age, tu illa loca proferas; siquidem tuæ hæ partes sunt. Tædet me μαλαμοδογιῶν, quæ sequentibus porro erotematis nectuntur. Proponis tibi erot. cxxxviii. & confingis loca S. scripturæ per universum S. contextum pro tuâ sententiâ sparsa: inde iterum bellissimam instituis quæstionem, an ergo de hac re secundum omnia illa & singula S. scripturæ loca, an istorum modo alialiqua judicandum sit? Nugæ venales. Si secundum aliqua, sic pergis, oportet rationes proferre; ut de iis cogitetur: quâ autem ratione qui id dicunt, sic certi esse possunt in suo illo ipsorum judicio? quum fieri possit, ut in aliis locis præteritis pro opposita parte plura dicantur, quam in locis, quæ adhibuerunt, dicuntur pro parte illâ, quam sequuti sunt. Et quo pacto tu in tuo judicio, vel aliquâ in re potes esse certus, quum fieri possit, ut plura pro opposita parte adferenda semper negligantur? hic ut tibi μετρον, oportet rationes proferre, ut de iis cogitetur. Sed missis tandem hisce τῶν ὁλῶς discutiendis, quod in Monsto non credo te aliâ ratione postulasse, quam quod probè noßes neminem tam firmi stomachi futurum, illud qui ferre posset: videamus quænam in tuâ Ecclesiâ Conniveнтiæ agi velis, quemque ordinem cultus publici observari.
units.tr: Erot. cxxxvi. But if you answer that there are such passages in Holy Scripture for erecting churches in this way, then it must be asked whether those passages of Holy Scripture lie in some one part of it, or are scattered here and there through the whole of the Holy Scripture's context? But now the answer is that nowhere in Scripture are there passages for your churches. Why then do you proceed with an untroubled and confident step, and, as if you were short of Holy Scripture passages, frame the question in this way? Here consider what you carelessly said in the Monitum: that it is indeed a case of prejudice from a preposterous cause, carried away with its own bogeys, that, in keeping with that party's spirit, they struggle and trifle, and want to persuade poor disciples who believe too readily of such things. I think you recognise your own words. Erot. cxxxvii. If it is said that those passages lie in some part of Holy Scripture, then those passages must be produced. Come, then, you produce them, since this is your business. I am weary of the wordy quibbles (μαλαμοδογιῶν) that the following erotemata go on to string together. You propose to yourself erot. cxxxviii., and you invent passages of Holy Scripture scattered through its whole context in support of your view. From this you again set up the very fine question whether the matter is to be judged according to all and each of the passages of Holy Scripture, or according to some of them only. Worthless trifles! If according to some, you go on thus: reasons must be produced, so that they may be considered; but by what reasoning can those who say this be so certain of their own judgment, since it may happen that in other passages passed over more is said for the opposite side than in the passages they adduced is said for the side they followed. And how can you be certain of your judgment, or of anything at all, since it may happen that more arguments for the opposite side are always neglected? Here is your measure: reasons must be produced, so that they may be considered. But, these questions of the whole (τῶν ὅλως) being at last set aside, which I do not believe you demanded in the Monitum for any other reason than that you knew well that no one would have a stomach strong enough to bear it, let us see what you wish to be done in your Church of Connivance, and what order of public worship is to be observed.

units.la: Ac primò quidem S. Scripturam unicè solo contextu, citra expositionem ullam, vel tractationem vult legi, Dei nomine. Vide erot. xlvi. verbum illud Dei scriptum prout est et jacet absque ullis ejus explicationibus.
units.tr: And first of all, you want Holy Scripture to be read solely as its bare text, without any exposition or treatment whatever, in the name of God. See erot. xlvi.: the word of God written, just as it is and lies, without any explanations of it.

units.la: Erot. I. nudum illæ verbi illius scripti audium, nomine Dei, &c. est unicum medium, & sufficit fidei ingenerandæ. Erot. lix. nudus auditus scripti illius verbi, prout verbum illud est, et just, absque ullis commentis, explicationibus aut glossis. erot. cvii. cxx. cx. Cum Dei institutione, mandato vel beneplacita permissione convenire, ut loco catechesium et confessionum illarum non ὁλῶς insite indubiè mereque verarum et non authenticarum substituatur in Ecclesiâ, nomine ut dictum est Dei, ipsissimum scriptum Dei verbum, tanquam authenticum, ac ὁλῶς insite indubiè mereque vera Christianorum prædictum in finem catechesis et confessio.
units.tr: Erot. I. The bare hearing of that written word, in the name of God, etc., is the only means and is sufficient to beget faith. Erot. lix. The bare hearing of that written word, as that word is, without any inventions, explanations or glosses. Erot. cvii., cxx., cx. It is in accordance with God's institution, command or permissive will that, in place of those catechisms and confessions, which are not wholly, infinitely, undoubtedly and truly genuine and authentic, there should be substituted in the Church, in the name of God, as has been said, the very text of God's word, as authentic, and wholly, infinitely, undoubtedly and truly the Christians' catechism and confession, for the end [of instruction].

units.la: Deinde etiam S. Scripturæ expositionem adhiberi permittit, sed non illam scilicet Dei nomine; at nomine Ecclesiæ, cujusque membrorum, ex vocatione non ullâ ad id singulari; sed communi omnium Christianorum, ut per exercitium Prophetiarum, quale I Cor. xiv. at-
units.tr: Next, it also permits the use of an exposition of Holy Scripture, but not, of course, in the name of God; rather in the name of the Church and of its members, by no singular calling to this, but by the common calling of all Christians, as through the exercise of prophecies, such as 1 Cor. 14, at-

units.la: quæ que non aliâ authoritate, vel nomine putat çtigi hoc defectivo statu Ecclesiam ullam posse. erot. cxxv i. Ut talis defectiva Ecclesia Ecclesias erigeret, colligeret, & regeret, non quidem Dei nomine, seu pro Deo legatione fingendo; sed authoritate duntaxat Ecclesiastica, nomine membrorum Ecclesia respectivorum, & jure vocationis communis. Erot. cxxxv i. exstare loca in S. script. literis ad Ecclesias (ut dictum est) authoritate duntaxat talis Christianissimi Ecclesiastica, jure communis talium Christianorum vocationis, etc. in Dei ut dictum est tolerantia & conniventia erigendas, colligendas & regendas. De collegio & exercitio Prophetico agit, erot. cl iv. in quo haec duo ponit, quae in concionibus nostris desiderat. i. ibi non aliquibus solum ad id ordinatis (uti in concionibus) sed universo populo licere agere, & ἀσφαλῶς. Quasi vero hoc quis neget, in exercitio Prophetico vel Catechetico licere aliis quoque loqui quam Pastoribus, & ἀσφαλῶς: vel istud conciones tollat, in quibus solus Concionator agit: sic enim in Veteri Judaica, ac primitiva Christiana simul & Concionum & Prophetiæ usus valuit, utrumque juxta, neque unum altero tollebatur, veli nimiçA Concionibus Prophetia erat, Unde utrumque in Ecclesiis nostris tenemus quantum fieri potest, urgemusque, vel ipso, quocum hic agimus, agnoscente Auctore, erot. clv i i i. Secundo carpit in concionibus nostris, quod emendare se in Prophetico suo profitetur, quod de quibuslibet promiscuè textibus audiantur apud nos conciones, ac quilibet Theologiæ articuli & puncta ibi tractentur; quum velit de aliquibus selectioribus modo locis ad populum atque ejus captum & aedificationem agi. In quo nobis quidem injuriam facit, quasi non populi & aedificationis Ecclesiae potissimam rationem haberemus, etiam in textibus seligendis, tractandisque pro captu & institutione ac salute auditorum; sed maxima fit injuria S. Scripturæ, quasi non etiam omnia quæ in ea, ad populi aedificationem exponi & tractari. stari queant, imò debeant. Neque denique haec observant in suis coetibus, qui ibi explicarunt nuperrimè librum & Prophetiam Danielis, tum Acta Apostolorum; potuissent etenim faciliora ad captum auditorum & notiora, forte etiam magis aedificantia alia ex S. libris tractare: vel haec si illi, & talem vel librum, vel caput integrum de quibuslibet eo contentis articulis promiscuè exponere queant, quid est, quod in nostris concionibus ultra reprehendunt, trabe in oculo ipsi laborantes κυριοπηγίαν? Sic habet erotemate clxv. Et solis sibi in Ecclesiâ (reliquo omni populo exclusò) loquendi jus faciunt, contra utriusque Ecclesiae tam veteris Iudaicae, quam indè ex parte mutuatum primitivae Christianae morem (quà de re inter alia videre est 1 Cor. 14. per totum; de quo suo loco); qui mos Ecclesiae primitivae Christianae subordinatus erat ἀλλὰ insitè indubiè mereque vera Apostolorum directioni; neque (ut ab evo hodieque in Ecclesiis, mediantibus concionibus perperam fit) quorumlibet contextum explicatione promiscua effectiva tali directione destituta, constabat. Atque erot. clvIII. sic de nobis loquitur: quibus hodiernis coetibus sese Dei nomine (attamen ex ignorantiâ) venditantibus, etiamsi ut dictum est imperfectis; quia inter alia destituuntur verbo orali praedicato ἀλλὰ insitè indubiè mereque vero, & praesumtuosis, qua verbum summum concionatorium non ἀλλὰ insitè indubiè mereque verum pro divino cultu, nomine Dei, seu Dei loco, & authoritate peracto, venditant; & soli ministri ibi loqui, & quidem de quibuslibet punctis volunt, Ecclesiarumque suarum omnem erectionem, collectionem, regimen ac disciplinam nomine Dei peragunt, &c. Atque ita in suis quoque coetibus sermonem & concionem ex Scripturâ S. admittit, & instituit, sermonem aedificationis publicae, uti appellat, quo, quae ex S. literis quis collegit ad publicam Ecclesiarum erectionem, cultum, regimen, & aedificationem facientia, omnibus, publicè communicat: quae proximè ad cultum & statum Ecclesiae infallibilem accedere gloriatur. Vide de hisce erot. clxxiv. Sin autem nihil hac de re proferatur: Tum quaerendum est, utrum, quam ipsissimae S. S. literae, prout sunt et iacent, publice offeruntur pro unica Dei ut dictum nomine Catechesi et confessione; pro unico item medio universi publici cultus, defectivo hoc Ecclesiae statu, per illas, nomine Dei, id est, quae medium pro Deo legatione fungendo, Ecclesiastica dumtaxat ut dictum est authoritate jure vocationis communis, et nomine membrorum Ecclesiae respectivorum in Dei ut dictum est tolerantia et conniventia, administrandi; item pro unico ὅλως infinite indubie mereque vero medio Ecclesiastici in communibus fundamentalibus regiminis, et mutuae itidem mediante sermone edificationis publicae, quae ipsi S. Scriptura subordinata, ac quoad exercitium, proxime ἀλλως infinite indubie mereque verae sint; pro debito item medio mutuae tolerantiae: Quum inquam ipsissimae SS litera ab aliquibus Christianis Deum timentibus, qui defectivo hoc Ecclesiae statu, universas SS. literas, quoad illam Ecclesiae in Dei tolerantia et conniventia erectionem, collectionem et regimen, pro et contra, ut dictum est, ruminati sunt, et collecta illa omnibus sincere communicarunt, praedicto modo publice offeruntur; et omnem Ecclesiarum erectio, collectio, cultus, aedificatio, regimen, ac tolerantia, juxta SS. literarum in collectis illis manifestissimam determinationem, Ecclesiastica ut dictum est dumtaxat authoritate, jure vocationis communis, et nomine membrorum Ecclesiae respectivorum, admissis semper gratoque animo manifestissime melioribus, unice comparitur; utrum tunc inquam homini Christiano praesentia prout optime poterit probanti, et sincere libereque approbanti, tempestivum, ac utile futurum sit, certe illi se adjungere, ad Deum uno cum pluribus animo publice colendum, laudandum, ac profitendum; proximumque invicem, mediante sermone, publice cum fundamentalibus illis communibus aedificandum: quo alii similiter agant; ut ita, pro ratione praesentium singulis talis Ecclesiae statibus donorum, voluntas Dei in terra ab omnibus fidelibus Christi
units.tr: ...which, without any other authority or name, they think a Church in this defective state can be erected. Erot. cxxvi. So that such a defective Church might erect, gather and govern Churches, not indeed by pretending to the name of God or an embassy on God's behalf, but by ecclesiastical authority only, in the name of the respective members of the Church, and by the right of common calling. Erot. cxxxvi. That there are in the passages of Holy Scripture, for churches (as has been said), by the authority of such a most Christian ecclesiastical body only, by the right of the common calling of such Christians, etc., to be erected, gathered and governed, by God's tolerance and connivance, as has been said. He treats of the college and the prophetic exercise in erot. cliv., in which he sets out these two things, which he misses in our sermons: first, that there it is lawful for the whole people, not merely for some men appointed to this (as in sermons), to act, and that without danger. As if anyone denied that in the prophetic or catechetical exercise it is lawful for others also to speak besides the ministers, and without danger; or as if he would abolish the sermons, in which the preacher alone acts. For in the old Jewish and in the primitive Christian Church the use of both sermons and prophecy held force together; each was observed alongside the other, and neither was abolished by the other; indeed prophecy was in some way superior to sermons. Hence we hold both in our Churches as far as possible, and we press them, and the author himself, with whom we are dealing here, acknowledges this. Secondly, he carps at our sermons, because he professes to correct in his prophetic exercise that in our churches sermons are heard on any texts indiscriminately, and any articles and points of theology are treated there, whereas he wishes that only certain more select passages be dealt with for the people, for their capacity and edification. In this he does us an injustice, as if we did not have the chief concern for the people and the edification of the Church, even in choosing and treating texts according to the capacity, instruction and salvation of the hearers. But the greatest injustice is done to Holy Scripture, as if all the things in it could not also be expounded and treated for the edification of the people, indeed ought to be. Nor do they observe these things in their own meetings, who have recently explained the book and prophecy of Daniel, and then the Acts of the Apostles; for they could have treated other, easier and better known, perhaps even more edifying, parts of the holy books. Or, if they themselves can expound indiscriminately any such book or whole chapter on any of the articles contained in it, why do they further reprehend in our sermons what they do, labouring under a beam in their own eye (κυριοπηγίαν)? Thus he says in erot. clxv.: And they claim for themselves alone the right to speak in the Church (all the rest of the people being excluded), against the custom of both the old Jewish Church and the primitive Christian Church, borrowed in part from it (on which matter, among other things, see 1 Cor. 14 throughout, to be treated in its place); which custom of the primitive Christian Church was subordinate to the wholly, infinitely, undoubtedly and truly genuine direction of the Apostles; nor did it consist (as is done wrongly from age to age and today in the Churches through sermons) in an indiscriminate effective explanation of any texts destitute of such direction. And erot. clxviii. speaks of us thus: Those who, by present-day meetings, boast themselves in the name of God (yet from ignorance), even though, as has been said, they are imperfect, because among other things they lack the oral preaching of the word which is wholly, infinitely, undoubtedly and truly genuine, and presumptuously, since they sell the chief preaching of the word, which is not wholly, infinitely, undoubtedly and truly genuine, as divine worship performed in the name of God, or in God's place, and by authority; and they want only the ministers to speak there, and indeed on any points whatever, and they perform every erection, gathering, governance and discipline of their Churches in the name of God, etc. And thus in their own meetings too he admits and institutes a discourse and sermon from Holy Scripture, a discourse of public edification, as he calls it, by which he publicly communicates to all whatever anyone has gathered from the holy letters that serves the public erection, worship, governance and edification of the Churches; things which he boasts come nearest to an infallible worship and state of the Church. See on these matters erot. clxxiv. But if nothing is produced on this matter, then it must be asked whether the very text of Holy Scripture, just as it is and lies, is publicly offered in the aforesaid way as the sole catechism and confession, in the name of God, that is, as the means of performing an embassy on God's behalf, to be administered by ecclesiastical authority only, as has been said, by the right of the common calling and in the name of the respective members of the Church, under God's tolerance and connivance; likewise as the sole wholly, infinitely, undoubtedly and truly genuine means of ecclesiastical governance in common fundamentals, and likewise, by the mutual means of a discourse of public edification, which, subordinate to Holy Scripture itself, and as to its exercise, are nearest to what is wholly, infinitely, undoubtedly and truly genuine; likewise as the due means of mutual tolerance. Since, I say, the very text of Holy Scripture, from certain Christians fearing God, who in this defective state of the Church have turned over all of Holy Scripture, as far as that erection, gathering and governance of the Church under God's tolerance and connivance goes, for and against, as has been said, and have communicated those collected things sincerely to all, is publicly offered in the aforesaid manner; and every erection, gathering, worship, edification, governance and tolerance of Churches, according to the most manifest determination of Holy Scripture in those collected things, is brought about solely by ecclesiastical authority, as has been said, by the right of the common calling, and in the name of the respective members of the Church, always admitting, with a grateful mind, things manifestly better; then, I ask, would it be timely and useful for a Christian man, who can prove it as well as he is able and approve it sincerely and freely, to join himself to these people, to worship, praise and profess God publicly together with many others, and mutually to edify his neighbour publicly by means of discourse, on those common fundamentals; so that others may likewise act in this way, and that, according to the measure of gifts present to each state of such a Church, the will of God on earth may be done unanimously by all the faithful of Christ, as it is done unanimously in heaven?

units.la: ais anis unanimiter fiat, quemadmodum unanimiter fit in cœlo? Breviter respondeo I. inane esse totum hoc ædificium ἀνθ' ἑνὸς μυρίων ἀπλῶς ἐπιτίθεται ἀξίωμα; nam quæsivisti quidem, at nunquam probasti, imò ne quidem probare aggressus es, S. literarum sufficientiam non ferre aliquas ex eâ desumtas & compositas Catecheses ac confessiones, vel concliones; nec Ecclesiæ Christianæ illum statum defectivum & apostaticum, quem fingis; Ecclesiam conniventiæ, &c. nobis demonstrasti. II. Contradicis, dum ex unâ parte asseris S. literas nomine Dei publicè legi, ac offerri; & deinde, ecclesiasticâ duntaxat authoritate, jure vocationis, & nomine membrorum ecclesiæ: siquidem ipse hæc hactenus sic opposuisti, ut verbi divini solum ac nudum contextum legi voluerIS nomine Dei; at ejus expositionem vel concionem, hoc Ecclesiarum statu, nec à nobis, neque à vobis, nomine Dei habendam; sed solum authoritate quadam Ecclesiasticâ: ergo quod duntaxat authoritate Ecclesiasticâ, & ex communi vocatione offertur, vel agitur; illud non quoque nomine Dei, juxta omnem tuam in totâ hac disputatione & perpetuam distinctionem inter nomine Dei quid agere, & nomine Ecclesiæ. Aliàs nos sic sentimus, utrumque bene convenire, ut Pastores nomine Dei, & nomine Ecclesiæ simul agant, verùm non tum dicimus illos concionari duntaxat authoritate Ecclesiastica, & jure vocationis communis contradistinctè & oppositè ad authoritatem Dei: interim tu ob illam sententiam nos censes apostaticos, iniquos, cœtus malignantium, & tantum non Antichristianos, III. Et in eo miserè impingis, quod pro eodem ponas, authoritate Ecclesiasticâ aliquid agere, & jure vocationis communis, & nomine membrorum Ecclesiæ: hæccine eadem? vocatio communis annon differt à vocatione ecclesiastica? numquid non vides? in mulieribus intuere, illi omnia habent, quæ ex vocatione communi Christianorum, & membrorum Ecclesiæ alicui debentur, tur, & tamen illis interdictum, ne in ecclesiâ loquantur; credo & sic in vestris coetibus. Vide mihi, vocatio communis, quare dicitur communis? unde hoc habet? inde simul manifestum fiet unde dicatur, & quid plus ac singulare habeat vocatio, & authoritas Ecclesiastica. Tum etiam aliud est, agere ut membrum ecclesiæ, pro jure membri; aliud, nomine membrorum ecclesiæ respectivorum: quæ imperitè confundis. IV. Explica, quodnam ecclesiasticum regimen intelligas & intendas, qui antea impotenter es debacchatus in Ecclesiarum Christianarum omne regimen; eoque, jure à te posco, aliud ac melius nobis ut commonstres. V. Quæ tibi communia fundamentalia, quorum hic non semel facis mentionem? VI. Quid, regimen in fundamentalibus? VII. Quare S. literæ dicuntur divinum unicumque medium Ecclesiastici in communibus fundamentalibus regiminis cur non regiminis totius Ecclesiastici, & in universum? quâ de causâ sic præcisè, in communibus fundamentalibus? VIII. Quando in tuâ Ecclesiâ, juxta verbum, pro stylo tuo ἁπλῶς insitè, indubiè merèque verum, ampullas, & sesquipedalia; addis, itidem mediante sermone edificationis publica, sive, quod idem est, verbum concionis; annon eadem omnia quæ adversum Conciones nostras, (missō, quod nomine Dei habentur) similiter locum habebunt contra tuam Ecclesiam vel sermonem ædificationis additum verbo divino? quomodo hic ferres, si diceremus à vobis supplementi loco addi, vel substitui divino, vestrum sermonem seu verbum orale, aut concionatorium, uti mavis loqui? qualia nobis & falsò & frustra exprobras. Vel missis hujusmodi ex sententiâ deductionibus, quid ultra habes, quod in nostris concionibus carpas, si eas ipse in tuis coetibus admittis? Si, quod apud nos verbum infallibile, per fallibiles, qua nos respicit, exponatur itidem apud vos? Dices, id apud nos fieri singulariter nomine Dei; quomodo hoc intelligendum sit, postea docebimus; inte-rim rim observetur, praecipuum esse, si non totum, modus agendi, quem in nobis censes, quod nomine Dei aliqua dicantur apud nos fieri, quae vos malitis fieri & dici nomine Ecclesiae. Unde iterum quaero, siquidem in eo errent Ecclesiae, tantum id, ut ideo & ob hoc solum omnes Ecclesias ab aevo Apostolorum huc usque censeas apostaticas, & nostras hodie ne quidem nomine Ecclesiae dignas, adeoque cunctas palam deserendas, anathematizandas? dixisti enim hominis Deum timentis animam nostras intrare non debere, quod satis grave in nos est anathema, ✡ ix. Dum dicis, S. literas medium esse unicum publici cultus, &c. mediante itidem sermone edificationis publicae; quaero, an hinc non eadem strui interrogationes & objectiones possint ad Scripturae arguendam insufficientiam, imperfectionem, obscuritatem, &c. quas inaniter antea ab eo t.lxv i i.& deinceps formasti hoc ex loco contra nostras conciones, & non retentum merum ac solum S. scripturae in coetibus, qui legeretur, contextum? Sic mihi jam liceat tibi reponere tua bellissima erotemata. lxx. Si responsum fuerit, quod praedicta illi insint; negari enim id utique jam nulla ratione potest: Tum quaerendum est; utrum pueruli in Christo, ex solo SS. literarum auditu, sive publico sive privato, qui Dei (ut dictum est) nomine adhibitus fuerit, hac illud suum; juvenes itidem panem suum, & patres vinum suum consequi possint absque ullo praeterea externo medio, Dei nomine, seu Dei loco & authoritate adhibito; nec ne? lxxi. Si dicatur, quod illi praedicta inde (ut dictum est) consequi non possint. Tum quaerendum est; utrum id accidat, aut propter S. scripturae quoad pueriulos juvenes & patres in Christo obscuritatem; aut propter diffusam S. scripturae latitudinem & amplitudinem; aut propter aliquod vetitum divinum; quo prohibeantur praedicti illi, ne rebus Christianismi sic stantibus, ex solo S. literarum ut dictum est auditu, hac, panem & vinum suum petant? Atque ita te tandem interrogo, quid est, quum tanto ni-
units.tr: Do you say it should happen unanimously on earth, just as it happens unanimously in heaven? I answer briefly. First, this whole edifice is empty: ἀνθ' ἑνὸς μυρίων ἀπλῶς ἐπιτίθεται ἀξίωμα [a single assertion is simply set against ten thousand]. For although you have asked, you have never proved, nor even attempted to prove, that Holy Scripture is insufficient and that catechisms and confessions, or sermons, drawn up from it are not needed. Nor have you shown us that the Christian Church is in the defective and apostate state you imagine, a Church of connivance and so on. Second, you contradict yourself. On the one hand you assert that Holy Scripture is publicly read and offered in the name of God, and on the other hand that it is done by ecclesiastical authority alone, by right of calling, and in the name of the members of the Church. For you have so set out your position up to now that only the bare text of the divine Word is to be read in the name of God, while its exposition or sermon, in the present state of the Churches, is to be held neither by us nor by you in the name of God, but only by a certain ecclesiastical authority. So what is done only by ecclesiastical authority and by common calling, that is not also done in the name of God. This follows from your whole distinction, constant throughout this dispute, between acting in the name of God and acting in the name of the Church. Otherwise we think both can well stand together, so that ministers act at once in the name of God and in the name of the Church. But we do not say that they preach merely by ecclesiastical authority and by right of common calling, set in contrast and opposition to the authority of God. Meanwhile, because of that opinion you judge us apostate, unjust, a company of wicked men, and almost antichristian. Third, you wretchedly stumble in this, in that you treat as the same thing acting by ecclesiastical authority and acting by right of common calling and in the name of the members of the Church. Are these the same? Does common calling not differ from ecclesiastical calling? Do you not see it? Look at women: they have all the things that are owed to any Christian by common calling and as members of the Church, and yet they are forbidden to speak in the church. I suppose it is the same in your assemblies. Tell me: why is the calling called common? Where does it get that name? From this it will at once become clear why it is so called, and what more and what peculiar thing the ecclesiastical calling and authority has. Moreover, it is one thing to act as a member of the Church, by the right of a member, and another to act in the name of the members of the Church as a whole; you confuse these carelessly. Fourth, explain what ecclesiastical government you understand and intend, you who earlier raged without restraint against all government of Christian Churches. I demand by right that you show us another and better one. Fifth, what are those common fundamentals, of which you make mention here more than once? Sixth, what is government in fundamentals? Seventh, why is Scripture called the divine and only means of ecclesiastical government in common fundamentals, and not of the whole ecclesiastical government, and in general? For what reason do you say precisely in common fundamentals? Eighth, when in your Church, according to the Word, in your own style ἁπλῶς [simply] and indubitably and purely true, you add, with your bombast and your long words, likewise by means of the sermon of public edification, or what is the same, the word of preaching: will not all the things you say against our sermons (setting aside that they are held in the name of God) apply equally against your Church, or against the sermon of edification added to the divine Word? How would you take it if we said that your sermon, or your oral or preaching word, as you prefer to call it, is added to or substituted for the divine Word as a supplement? These are the things you falsely and vainly charge us with. Or, setting aside such deductions from your opinion, what else do you have to criticise in our sermons, if you yourself admit them in your own assemblies? If the infallible Word is expounded through fallible men among us, as it is in the sense in which you regard us, is it not likewise so among you? You will say that this happens among us in a special way, in the name of God. How this is to be understood we will teach later. Meanwhile, let it be noted that the principal thing, if not the whole, is the mode of acting that you think we follow, namely that some things are said among us in the name of God which you would rather have done and said in the name of the Church. So I ask again: if the Churches err in this, and only in this, do you therefore, and for this alone, judge all Churches from the age of the Apostles until now to be apostate, and ours today not even worthy of the name of Church, and therefore all of them openly to be deserted and anathematised? For you have said that the soul of a God-fearing man must not enter our assemblies, which is a sufficiently grave anathema against us. Ninth, when you say that Holy Scripture is the sole means of public worship, and so on, likewise mediated by the sermon of public edification, I ask whether the same questions and objections cannot be built from this place to argue the insufficiency, imperfection, obscurity and so on of Scripture, which you earlier vainly framed from the same place against our sermons, and which you did not keep to the bare and sole text of Holy Scripture read in the assemblies. Thus let me now answer your very fine questions in return. Question 70: If it is answered that the aforesaid things are contained in it, for this can by no means be denied: then it must be asked whether little children in Christ can obtain their bread, and young men their bread, and fathers their wine, by the mere hearing of Holy Scripture alone, whether public or private, which is used in the name of God (as was said), without any further external means used in the name of God or in place of God and by his authority; or not? Question 71: If it is said that those aforesaid things cannot be obtained from it (as was said), then it must be asked whether this happens because of the obscurity of Holy Scripture for little children, young men and fathers in Christ, or because of the wide extent and amplitude of Holy Scripture, or because of some divine prohibition by which those aforesaid persons are forbidden, while Christianity stands as it does, to seek their bread and wine from the mere hearing of Holy Scripture, as was said? And so I finally ask you: what is it, when you press so hard against us the mere and bare hearing of the infallible divine Word in the Churches, apart from all exposition, that you do not likewise use the same hearing in your own assemblies, and the bare Holy Scripture without any of its expositions?

units.la: su contra nos urgeas solum ac merum auditum verbi divini infallibilis in Ecclesiis citra omnem expositionem, illum non sic quoque adhibeas in vestris coetibus, & meram scripturam sacram, nullas ejus expositiones?
units.tr: You press against us the mere and bare hearing of the infallible divine Word in the Churches, apart from all exposition. Do you not likewise use it in your own assemblies, the bare Holy Scripture with no exposition of it?

units.la: x. Qua ratione tuum sermonem concionatorium appellas proxime ὅλως insite indubie merèque verum? an remotior est a fallibilitate, & proximior infallibilitati nostrae? Ostende gradus inter fallibile & infallibile, vel indubie verum, ac dubie verum. Recte attende, non quaero gradus veritatis, sed gradus infallibilitatis, contrapositè ad fallibilitatem. Et quare tua concio vel ille sermo propior est divino infallibili, quam nostep? praesertim si materialiter eundem consideremus. Sane haec non ponenda, & in gratiam tuam effingenda atque sic leviter fuerant, sed aliquo saltem indicio comprobanda.
units.tr: Tenth. By what reasoning do you call your preaching sermon, which is ὅλως insite [wholly implanted] and indubitably and purely true, closer to fallibility and nearer to infallibility than ours? Show the degrees between the fallible and the infallible, or between what is indubitably true and what is doubtfully true. Pay close attention: I am not asking for degrees of truth, but for degrees of infallibility, set over against fallibility. Why is your sermon, or that discourse, closer to the divine infallible than ours is, especially if we consider them as to their matter, which is the same? Certainly these things should not have been laid down and fashioned lightly for your sake, but should at least have been supported by some indication.

units.la: xi. Quam intelligis mutuam tolerantiam, & cujus tuus aedificationis publicae sermo sit debitum medium? xii. Non est in dictis illis completus sensus: quum inquam ipsissima S S. litera ab aliquibus Christianis Deum timentibus, nam inde incipit parenthesis prolixissima, qui defectivo hoc, &c. usque ad aliud inquam, quod sequitur, verum tum inquam, homini Christiano, &c. & quo priora illa spectent, non video: quod nullus miror tibi contigisse in scripto tam longis ac otiosis periphrasibus ac parenthesibus constipato.
units.tr: Eleventh. What mutual tolerance do you understand, and of what is your sermon of public edification the due means? Twelfth. The sense is not complete in those words. When I say, the very Holy Scripture, by some Christians who fear God (for there begins a very long parenthesis, who in this defective state, and so on, down to the other thing which follows, true, then, I say, to a Christian man, and so on), I do not see to which of the earlier words those belong. I am not surprised that this happened to you, in a writing so crammed with such long and idle periphrases and parentheses.

units.la: xiii. Teipsum dein mire depraedicas, tuumque studium in conferenda S. Scriptura, illamque quoad Ecclesiae tuae erectionem pro & contra ruminanda, & quod maxime mirum, hic jam commentarios scripturae, omniaque alia adminicula adhiberi, quae alibi indigne explodis. erotem. cxlviii. pag. 64. Contra e rot. cxl. vult loca Scripturae examinari, tam illa quae sunt τὰ ἐντὸς, quàm illa quae sunt τὰ ἔξω ἀλλόσιας, ex ipsissimis S S. literis universis, juxta linguas earum originales, paraphrases Chaldaicas, versiones Graecam, Syriacam, Arabicam, Aethiopicam, Armenicam, &c. (quandoquidem haec res omnes Christianos dictam defectionem passos, concernit,) item adhibitis tam veteribus, quam recentioribus, Ebrais, Græcis, Latinis, aliarumque linguarum in SS. Literas commentariis ceterisque admonitionibus, tum literariis, tum præcipue spiritualibus. Effare nunc, quo pacto illa putes sciri ac haberi posse, nisi scholæ, &c. maneant, quas etiam illo ereæ exlvi ii. eliminas. Sed quod addis, eadem collectanea omnibus sincerè communicanda esse, ut omnis Ecclesiarum erectio, collectio, cultus, ædificatio, regimen, ac tolerantia, juxta SS. literarum in collectis illis manifestissimam determinationem, mutuò componatur; hoc egregiam sapit arrogantiam. Nam r. tu ille es, qui adeò excarnificas confessiones Ecclesiarum, & catecheses, formulas liturgiarum, & acta regiminis Ecclesiastici presbyterialia, classicalia, synodalia, &c. & jam tuæ cudis systema collectaneorum (quod, quæso, in quo specificè differt à confessione aliquâ, vel catechesi, aut liturgiâ?) juxta quod omnem Ecclesiæ erectionem, cultum, regimen, &c. vis componi. ii. Quis judicabit, & assentiet tibi illam tuorum collectaneorum veritatem esse manifestissimam? hoc ubi negaverit aliquis, ut nihil ferme est quantumcunque manifestæ veritatis, quod in dubium non trahatur, quid tuis, illis fiet? vel defini, quam manifestissimam veritatem appelles, an forte cum Remonstrantibus illam, quæ apud omnes in confesso, quibus modò sanum sincipit, quæque in Christianismo, quam latè patet, nec controversa, neque controverti possunt. iii. Et quando tuis longè & manifestissimè meliora, forte adferemus, neque tu tamen, tuique (non enim puto jactabis vel spondebis omnes tuos tam probæ indolis semper esse, ut nunquam veritati sint refragaturi,) nostra grato animo admiserint; quid tum sperabimus, quidve inde oritur, nisi antiquum disputare, concedere, secedere? quod ergo nec tuo remedio correxeris, quin sic valdè etiam adauxeris. Sed satis diu opinor hor in hoc uno erotemate enodando hæsimus; unde iu- dica, quantum operis in te exposcas, si, quod in Monito jubes, tua singula erotemata pedeprestim examinare, atque digne refutare instituerimus. Eadem quæ in hoc erotemate, pro more repetuntur erot. clxxv i, ubi cætus sui cultum sic describit: ad cultum naturâ sua pacificum. Ecclesiastica quidem duntaxat ut dictum authoritate, jure vocationis communis, & nomine membrorum Ecclesiæ respectivorum, in Dei (ut dictum est) tolerantiâ & connivantiâ erectum; attamen per ipsissimum ὅλως insite indubie mereque verum verbum Dei scriptum, per medium regiminis, mutuæ mediante sermone ædificationis publica, ac tolerantia, in verbo illo, ὅλως insite indubie mereque vera, & quoad exercitium proxime ὅλως insite indubie mereque vera, peractum, tam ministerium quam populus perducti sunt. quæ si iterum ad partes revocarem, non minus intricata & vitiosa apparerent, quam præcedentia, quale est, quod media regiminis in Ecclesiâ suâ vocat in verbo Dei mere vera, nisi forte vitium typographicum sit pro, vero. & quoad exercitium proximè indubie vera; quæ quid sibi velint, vix aliquis assequatur. 1. quomodo illa tua regiminis media queant dici infallibilia, vel indubie vera? 11. tum, proximè indubie mereque vera? χρυσοχυλοπλαστα.
units.tr: xiii. Then you lavishly praise yourself and your zeal in weighing Holy Scripture, turning it over for and against the erection of your Church. What is most remarkable is that you now admit commentaries on Scripture and all the other aids, which you elsewhere rejecte with contempt. Question 148, page 64. On the other hand, in question 140 you want the passages of Scripture to be examined, both those that are within and those that are outside the [canon], from the very text of all the Holy Scriptures according to their original languages, the Chaldee paraphrases, the Greek, Syriac, Arabic, Ethiopic and Armenian versions, and so on, since this matter concerns all Christians who have suffered the said defection. You also want the commentaries of Hebrews, Greeks and Latins, and of other languages, on the Holy Scriptures, and the other helps, both literary and especially spiritual, to be used. Tell us now how you think those things can be known and possessed, unless schools and so on remain, which you also remove in question 142. But when you add that this same collection should be sincerely shared with everyone, so that the erection, gathering, worship, building, government and toleration of all Churches may be mutually arranged according to the most evident determination of Scripture in those collections, this tastes of remarkable arrogance. For first, you are the one who so butchers the confessions of the Churches, the catechisms, the liturgical forms, and the acts of ecclesiastical government, presbyterial, classical, synodal and so on; and now you forge a system of collections of your own. (What, I ask, does it differ in kind from some confession, catechism or liturgy?) By this system you wish every erection, worship, government and so on of the Church to be arranged. Second, who will judge, and agree with you, that the truth of your collections is most evident? When someone denies this, as scarcely anything, however clearly true, is not called into doubt, what will become of your collections? Either define what you mean by "most evident truth", or perhaps you mean with the Remonstrants that truth which is agreed by all whose sense is sound, and which in Christianity, as far as it extends, is neither disputed nor can be disputed. Third, when we perhaps offer things far better and more evident than yours, you and yours (for I do not think you will boast or promise that all your people are always of such good disposition that they will never oppose the truth) will not receive ours with a grateful mind. What then shall we hope for, or what will come of it, except the old quarrel: dispute, yield, withdraw? Therefore you will not correct the matter by your remedy, but will rather greatly increase it in this way. But I think we have been stuck long enough on this one question. From this, judge how much work you demand if, as you order in the Admonition, we are to undertake to examine each of your questions step by step and refute them properly. The same things that are repeated in this question, as is your custom, recur in question 175, where you describe the worship of your gathering thus: worship peaceful by its nature. Indeed erected by ecclesiastical authority alone, as has been said, by the right of common calling, and in the name of the respective members of the Church, in the toleration and connivance of God (as has been said); yet, through the most intrinsically, undoubtedly and purely true word of God written, by the means of government, by public edifying speech in mutual exchange, and by toleration, in that word, intrinsically, undoubtedly and purely true, and as to its exercise, very nearly intrinsically, undoubtedly and purely true, accomplished, both the ministry and the people have been brought along. If I were again to take these words apart, they would appear no less tangled and faulty than the preceding ones. Such is your claim that in your Church the means of government are in the word of God purely true, unless perhaps it is a typographical error for "true". And as to its exercise, very nearly undoubtedly true; what these words mean hardly anyone could grasp. (1) How can those means of your government be called infallible, or undoubtedly true? (2) Then, very nearly undoubtedly and purely true? Golden-juice-moulded nonsense [χρυσοχυλοπλαστα].

units.la: Hactenus in deludro versati, lustravimus coetum Conniventiæ: superest, ut nos eadem opera edocuisses de statu ecclesiæ Christianæ, post apostaticam, conniventiæ illo, quo vera ecclesia erigenda per verbum iterum ὅλως infallibile exspectetur, & Apostolica demum reditura Ecclesia, idemque qui in Apostolis spiritus, verbum ὅλως insite indubie mereque verum, & par Ecclesiæ regimen, &c. quæ necdum scripto explicuisti, indicas tamen, credo quia hac vice nos ad nauseam satiatos prævidebas de Ecclesiarum præsenti statu tum apostasiæ, tum conniventiæ μωρᾶς ζητήσεως. Venimus igitur ad propositum: hoc enim dirigebamus, & hoc præstitiebimus, ad locutionis præfationem, ut jam hinc de eo congredia- mur, de quo adversarii provocant, ut cum Tertulliano loquar lib. de præscript. adv. hæret. Tempus ergo, ut ad disputandum me accingam, & argumenta quæ contra sententiam Adversarii faciunt, adferam; quamvis jam plura observari potuerint inter sententiæ indagationem sparsa, quæ pro re nata se certatim ac sponte obtulerunt: neque, ut in Commentario nostro de Weigelianis etiam monui, alia fere ratione confutari merentur hujusmodi hominum otiosorum, & schismaturientium phantasmata, quam eorundem plana & genuina expositione. Cyprianus, de unit. eccles. in initio: intellectus tamen est, & retusus, & ideo prostratus, quia agnitus, & detectus. Vel si quid praterea velis, & argumentari poscas; sufficit ad absurdum deducere, & εἰς ἀπόπον absurditatum ex sententia illorum continuo fluxu derivare. Parum abest, (nisi forte ex Auctore nostro, ejusque aëre, in quo versor & ludor, aliquantulum infectus, & jactabundus videar,) parum dico, abest, quin arbitrer erotematis hisce, vel sententiæ quam decerimus, factum sanè eorundem discussione, & super Controversia intelligenda habita jam οὐζήτησις quamvis nihil ultra adderem; hæc autem est, meo judicio, & sic proponenda censeo, quæstio:
units.tr: Having so far wandered in the mire, we have surveyed the gathering of Connivance. It remains that, in the same work, you should have informed us about the state of the Christian Church after the apostasy, under that connivance by which a true Church is to be erected again through the word, once more wholly infallible, and the Apostolic Church is at last to return, with the same Spirit as was in the Apostles, a word wholly infallible, undoubtedly and purely true, and an equal government of the Church, and so on. These things you have not yet explained in writing, but you indicate them, I believe, because this time you foresaw that we would be satiated to the point of nausea by your present state of the Churches, both of apostasy and of connivance, a foolish inquiry [μωρᾶς ζητήσεως]. We therefore come to the point. For this is what we were aiming at, and this we shall perform: to come, as the prefatory address puts it, now to the matter on which our adversaries challenge us, to use Tertullian's words in the book On Prescription against Heretics. It is time, then, for me to gird myself for disputation and bring forward the arguments that tell against the opinion of the adversary, although many points may already have been noticed, scattered through the investigation of the opinion, which offered themselves eagerly and spontaneously as the matter arose. Nor, as I also noted in our commentary on the Weigelians, do the fantasies of such idle and schismatic men deserve to be refuted by any other method than by their plain and genuine exposition. Cyprian, On the Unity of the Church, at the beginning: it is understood, and so it is refuted and laid low, because it has been recognised and exposed. Or if you want something further and demand that we argue it, it is enough to reduce it to absurdity and to derive from their opinion a continual flow of absurdities [εἰς ἄτοπον]. It hardly lacks (unless perhaps I seem somewhat tainted by our author, and by the air in which I move and play, and boastful) that I think that these questions, or the opinion we are to decide, have already been, by their discussion and by the debate about understanding the controversy, a full investigation, even though I would add nothing more. This, in my judgment, is the question, and I think it should be put thus:

units.la: Verum Ecclesiæ Christianæ Catholicæ, sive quæ in orbe sunt omnes, fuerunque ab ævo Apostolorum hucusque, à primis earum initiis sint apostaticæ, eo quod in illis Verbum Dei infallibile Veteris ac Novi Testamenti exponatur à ministris & concionibus non item infallibilibus, & tamen nomine Dei? Affirmat Auctor libelli ad legem & ad Testimonium, quocum impræsentiarum agimus: negant omnes Ecclesiæ. Argumentari hic, quod quidem facile possum, sive ex natura Ecclesiæ, aut concionum, vel ex ratione ministrorum ecclesiæ, aut S. Scripturæ, aut salutis. æternæ, aliisque locis, non est mihi animus, ratione jam dixi: solum ostendam infinita, quæ ex hac sententia ebulliunt, incommoda & absurda, breviter etiam, nam vel indicasse loca sufficerit, quæ cognita urgeri facile à quovis possunt. Decurremus autem nostra argumentatione juxta quatuor ab Auctore confictos Ecclesiarum status, Apostolicum, Apostaticum, Conniventiæ, & denique iterum Apostolicum.
units.tr: Are the Christian Churches, Catholic, that is, all that are in the world and have existed from the age of the Apostles until now, apostate from their first beginnings, because in them the infallible Word of God, of the Old and New Testament, is set forth by ministers and sermons that are not likewise infallible, and yet in the name of God? The author of the pamphlet To the Law and to the Testimony, with whom we are now dealing, affirms this; all the Churches deny it. I am not minded to argue this here, as I could easily do, whether from the nature of the Church or of sermons, or from the office of the ministers of the Church, or from Holy Scripture, or from eternal salvation, and in other places. I have already spoken of these matters for reasons. I will only show the countless inconveniences and absurdities that boil up from this opinion, briefly as well, for it will suffice to indicate the passages, which anyone can easily press once they are known. We shall run through our argument in accordance with the four states of the Churches that the author has invented: the Apostolic, the Apostate, that of Connivance, and finally the Apostolic again.

units.la: 1. Argum. Probandum Auctori primò fuerat, vel semper prædicationem verbi divini in Ecclesiâ continuari debuisse à ministris, æquè ac Apostoli infallibiliter seu ὁλως infitè indubiè mereque verè docentibus; vel peccari tum, quando verbum Dei à Ministris & Præconibus non infallibilibus, quales Apostoli, tractatur & exponitur: sive, jussisse Deum, ut non aliter, ejus nomine à quoquam verbum suum pro concione explicaretur ac doceretur, quam qui sermonem æquè infallibilem, ac illud Dei verbum, haberet. Nisi enim hoc certò & manifestè probetur à Deo mandatum, vel peccari secus agendo, frustra est omne quod molitur & crepat Auctor de Ecclesiis hac in re non peccantibus solum, sed imò apostaticis. Proba ante omnia, peccatum in eo committi. Iam verò verbum Dei exponi etiam posse à ministris non infallibilibus, ipse fatetur, dum in suis Conniventiæ cœtibus, sermonem publicæ ædificationis (uti vidimus) admittit, ac frequentat, eumque judicio Auditorum sic submittit, ut corrigi ac emendari posse, quin etiam debere aliquando, concedat: Atque etiam à Doctoribus fallibilibus verbum divinum prædicari nomine Dei, agnoscit in ministris particularium Ecclesiarum ævo Apostolico qui erant, Act. xi. xii. quod pro Christo legatione fungebantur, & genuinum illud unici Euangelii verbum prædicabant, ubi S. Scripturæ loca indifferenter pro illorum & Apostolorum functionibus adfert, quibus Apostoli de se ac suâ ministrorumque Euangelii legatione communiter loquunquantur: adeò nulla proferri possunt ex sacris documenta, quæ in isthoc formali, nomine Dei loquendo, differentiam istam constituunt inter Apostolos, doctores infallibiles, & inter Ecclesiarum ministros reliquos, qui dono infallibilitatis carentes, tamen docent idem Dei verbum. Sed personæ, inquit eror. xir. quæ nuncupato illud Evangelii verbum pro Deo legatione fungendo prædicare debebant & poterant, eâ in re ab invicem discrepabant, quod quedam illarum pro Deo legatione fungendo, in verbi illius merâ puritate semper starent, & ab eâ deflectere sive consciè sive insciè nec vellent, nec possent; quales erant Apostoli, eorumque similes: quædam autem illarum personarum pro Deo legatione fungendo, aut in verbi illius merâ puritate stare, & vel consciè vel insciè deflectere possent; quales erant prefati illi particularium Ecclesiarum ministri. Ergò discrimen ministrorum particularium, & Apostolorum, utrisque verbum Dei docentibus, non in eo consistit, an nomine Dei alii, alii aliter & duntaxat nomine Ecclesiæ doceant, uti nostri vult, sed quod infallibiles hi, illi vero fallibiles sunt. Materialiter idem verbum docetur ab utrisque, infallibile; sed non formaliter eodem modo infallibilitatis. Quibus sic se habentibus, ego non video, quid adeò in Ecclesiis nostris carpere Adversarius possit, quod verbum Dei, cujus nomine, quamvis non infallibiliter prædicatur. Et hoc tamen fundamentum habet totius sui molimínis; ac ...
units.tr: 1. Argument. The author should first have proved either that the preaching of the divine word in the Church ought always to have been continued by ministers, just as the Apostles taught infallibly, or wholly infallibly, undoubtedly and purely truly; or else that sin is committed when the word of God is handled and expounded by ministers and heralds who are not infallible, such as the Apostles were; or, that God commanded that his word should not be explained or taught in public in his name by anyone except one who had a discourse equally infallible as that word of God. For unless it is clearly and manifestly proved that this was commanded by God, or that sin is committed by acting otherwise, all that the author labours at and boasts of concerning Churches that not only do not sin in this matter but are even apostate is in vain. First of all, prove that sin is committed in it. Now, the author himself admits that the word of God can also be expounded by ministers who are not infallible, since in his gatherings of Connivance he admits and frequents public edifying speech (as we have seen), and submits it to the judgment of the hearers in such a way that he concedes it can be corrected and amended, and indeed sometimes ought to be. And he acknowledges that the divine word is also preached in the name of God by fallible teachers, in the ministers of particular Churches in the Apostolic age, who were Acts 11 and 12, who performed the office of Christ's ambassadors and preached that genuine word of the one Gospel. Moreover, he brings forward passages of Scripture indifferently for their functions and those of the Apostles, in which the Apostles commonly speak of themselves and of their ministers' embassy of the Gospel. Thus no documents can be brought from the sacred writings that, in this formal speaking "in the name of God," establish that difference between the Apostles, as infallible teachers, and the remaining ministers of the Churches, who, lacking the gift of infallibility, nevertheless teach the same word of God. But the persons, says Error 12, "who were to preach that word of the Gospel, in discharging the embassy of God, differed from one another in this, that some of them, in discharging the embassy of God, always stood in the pure truth of that word, and neither wished nor were able to depart from it, consciously or unconsciously; such were the Apostles and those like them. Others of those persons, in discharging the embassy of God, could stand in the pure truth of that word, and could depart from it consciously or unconsciously; such were the aforesaid ministers of particular Churches." Therefore the difference between the ministers of particular Churches and the Apostles, both teaching the word of God, does not consist in whether some teach in the name of God and others otherwise and merely in the name of the Church, as our author wants, but in that the one are infallible and the others fallible. Materially the same word is taught by both, infallible; but not formally in the same manner of infallibility. With matters standing thus, I do not see what the adversary can find to carp at in our Churches, since the word of God, in whose name it is preached, though not infallibly preached... And yet this has the foundation of his whole endeavour: ...

units.la: II. Argum. Dato, Ecclesias Christianas in eo peccare, quod nomine Dei concionentur eo modo, id est, non infallibiliter, probandum secundo loco fuerat (tuarum enim partium sunt hæc ostendere, & præstruere evidentissime, antequam consilium de mutandis & deserendis Ecclesiis, deque aliâ erigendâ capias ullum) probandum, dico, tibi erat, peccatum illud, quodcunque hac in re committant Ecclesiæ, tam grave ac nefandum esse, ut ideo Apostasia eamque solum vel potissimùm ob causam, Ecclesiis omnibus impingenda sit, eaque apostasia, quæ 1 Thess. 2. describitur, quæque mysterium iniquitatis καθ' ἐνέργειαν appellatur. Explicandus fuerat totus hic de apostasiâ locus, & applicandus nostris concionibus, ut pateret, quo jure, quâve injuriâ omnes Christianismi Ecclesiæ apostasiæ notâ ab Auctore inurantur atque condemnentur. Si hæc tibi apostasia, quis ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ὁ ἀντικείμενος, &c. quid, τὸ κατέχον? quid, quod istius hominis παρουσία καθ' ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ &c. dicitur? Notum, quod hic locus à Theologis accipitur de Antichristo, & Papæ Romano à Reformatis applicatur; si tu aliam velis ejus ἑρμηνείαν, aliumque Antichristum, explica; sed simul proba: neque enim nobis aut Elias, aut Pythagoras es. Non ob aliquod in genere peccatum, etiam aliquanto gravius, apostasiæ crimen nemini alicui intentandum; nisi tale sit, quod totius Christianæ fidei repudium secum ferat, qualis apostasia ad Mahumedilmum, aut Iudaismum, &c. vel quodcunque ei proximum, & Christianismi fundamenta prorsus convellit. An verò tibi tanti hoc videatur delictum, quod in Ecclesiis Christianis carpis, si modò delictum dicendum, ut apostasiam æquet, tute in conscientiâ coram Deo judica, & siquidem pertinaciter in illâ tuâ opinione perseveres, nobis distinctè ac evidenter demonstra.
units.tr: II. Argument. Granting that the Christian Churches sin in this, that they preach in God's name in such a way, that is, not infallibly, you should in the second place have proved (for it is your business to show these things and establish them very clearly before you take any step toward abandoning or deserting the Churches, or erecting another in their place) I say you should have proved that whatever fault the Churches commit in this matter is so grave and abominable that apostasy must be charged against all the Churches for this reason alone, or chiefly for this reason. And it should have been that apostasy which is described in 2 Thess. 2 and called the mystery of iniquity [μυστήριον τῆς ἀνομίας] working "according to the energy of Satan" [καθ' ἐνέργειαν]. The whole passage on apostasy should have been explained and applied to our sermons, so that it would be clear by what right, and with what injustice, all the Churches of Christendom are branded and condemned by the Author with the mark of apostasy. If this is the apostasy, who is "the man of sin" [ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας], "the son of perdition" [ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας], "the adversary" [ὁ ἀντικείμενος], etc.? What is "that which restrains" [τὸ κατέχον]? And what of the fact that the coming of that man is said to be "according to the working of Satan" [κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ], etc.? It is well known that this passage is taken by theologians to refer to Antichrist, and that the Reformed apply it to the Roman Pope. If you wish to offer another interpretation of it and another Antichrist, explain it; but at the same time prove it, for you are neither Elijah nor Pythagoras to us. No one should be charged with the crime of apostasy on account of some sin of a general kind, even a rather grave one, unless it is such that it carries with it a repudiation of the whole Christian faith, as apostasy to Mohammedanism or Judaism does, or anything close to it that utterly overturns the foundations of Christianity. But whether you yourself think this fault that you find in the Christian Churches (if it must be called a fault) is so great as to equal apostasy, you must judge in your own conscience before God; and if you persist stubbornly in that opinion, demonstrate it to us clearly and distinctly.

units.la: III. Argum. Illa si vera, quæ de Ecclesiæ Christianæ apostasiâ sentit Adversarius, sequetur, Ecclesias statim à tempore Apostolorum, formaliter fuisse apostaticas; nam cum excelsu Apostolorum desierunt Doctores Ecclesiæ infallibiles; imò jam illis adhuc superstitious bus multi verbum Dei tradiderunt, etiam nomine Dei, non tamen infallibiliter: qui ideóque non minùs imperfecti & præsumtuosi æstimari debent, quam reliqui, quibus eam ob causam dicam apostasiæ & iniquitatis scribit Noster; pro imperfectis quidem, quia inter alia ministri miseri eorum destituuntur verbo oralí ὅλως insitè indubiè in- rèque vero, quod Dei nomine in publico suo cultu proserant; pro præsumtuosis autem, quia nihilominus verbum suum concionatorium non ὅλως insitè indubiè mereque ve- rum, loco verbi ὅ λως insitè indubiè mereque veri, quod Dei ut dictum est nomine, publico in cultu uni è proferri debet, substituunt. Quum tamen, quamvis mysterium iniquitatis ac apostasiæ etiam ævo Apostolorum operari capisse fuerimus, nemo tamen dixerit, formalem jam tunc fuisse Ecclesiarum apostasiam.
units.tr: III. Argument. If what the Adversary thinks about the apostasy of the Christian Church were true, it would follow that the Churches were formally apostate from the very time of the Apostles. For once the Apostles had passed away, the teachers of the Church ceased to be infallible; indeed, even while those Apostles were still living, many men handed on the word of God, even in God's name, yet not infallibly. These men ought therefore to be judged no less imperfect and presumptuous than the rest, on whom our author for that reason charges apostasy and iniquity: imperfect, because among other things these poor ministers lacked the oral word that was wholly [ὅλως], indubitably and purely true, which they were to put forward in the name of God in public worship; presumptuous, because nevertheless they substituted their own preaching, which was not wholly, indubitably and purely true, in place of the word that, as has been said, ought to be proclaimed in public worship in the name of God, which was wholly, indubitably and purely true. Yet although we have granted that the mystery of iniquity and apostasy had already begun to work even in the age of the Apostles, no one will say that the Churches were then formally apostate.

units.la: IV. Argum. Sequetur insuper apostasiam & quidquid mali illa continet, ab Apostolis ipsis, ne dicam à Christo, originem suam trahere, iisque ejus causam assignandam, quod ordinarint in Ecclesiâ Pastores non infallibiles semper, sed qui verbum Dei exponerent verbo oralinon ὅλως insit, indubiéque vero, atque sic apostasiam ipsi fundarint. Quum enim de Christo dicltur, quod dederit Ecclesiæ hos quidem Apostolos, illos vero Prophetas, illos vero Evangelistas, illos vero Pasto- res & Doctores, Ephes. IV. 11. non additur Pastores, ac Doctores fore perpetuum infallibiles, & Apostolis in eo similes: namque ista pacto discrimen Apostolo- rum & reliquorum Doctorum, quod ipse quoque agnoscis, & in infallibilitate constitutis, erat. XVII. tolletur.
units.tr: IV. Argument. It would further follow that apostasy, and whatever evil it contains, has its origin in the Apostles themselves, not to say in Christ, and that the cause of it must be assigned to them, because they ordained in the Church ministers who were not always infallible, but who expounded the word of God by an oral word that was not wholly, indubitably and purely true, and so they themselves founded the apostasy. For when it is said of Christ that he gave to the Church some as Apostles, some as Prophets, some as Evangelists, and some as Pastors and Teachers (Eph. 4:11), it is not added that the Pastors and Teachers would be perpetually infallible and like the Apostles in this respect. For in that case the distinction between the Apostles and the other teachers, which you yourself acknowledge, and which consisted in infallibility, would be abolished.

units.la: V. Argum. Tales Doctores & præcones verbi di- vini, qui Scripturam exposuerunt in Ecclesiâ, Dei no- mine, non infallibiliter semper fecerunt in Ecclesiâ & olim, neque tamen unquam vel in V. Testamento, vel à Christo sub Novo, aut Apostolis eo solùm nomine, posito quod vera docuerint, pro apostatis habiti, reprehensi vel damnati fuerunt unquam, vel Ecclesiæ idcirco judicatæ apostaticæ. Ergò.
units.tr: V. Argument. Such teachers and heralds of the divine word, who expounded Scripture in the Church in God's name without always being infallible, have done so in the Church both in ancient times and now; yet they were never, either in the Old Testament, or under the New Testament by Christ or the Apostles, regarded as apostates, rebuked or condemned on that ground alone, namely that they taught what was true, nor were the Churches for that reason judged apostate. Therefore...

units.la: VI Argum. Sequetur, omnes in orbe Ecclesias Christianas à temporibus Apostolorum usque esse ac fuisse formaliter apostaticas, ut in quibus non aliter concionatum Dei verbum fuit, quod quamvis leviter & nulla opera digerere valeat noster, mihi tamen, ac profecto dubio omnibus Christianis tam horrendum audire est, ut nihil supra, argumentique loco in contrarium, quod tale aliud potius sit, quam istud. Verum quidem apostasiam Antichristianam multam Orbis partem ac diu occupasse, sed nihilominus & plures hic illic fuerunt semper in Oriente atque in Occidente Ecclesiæ, cœtus & fideles, qui contrà senserint omnibus sæculis, & veritatem sacrosanctam custodierint. Ita dicere, & tam facile, omnes omnino Ecclesias ab omni retro antiquitate apostaticas!
units.tr: VI. Argument. It would follow that all the Christian Churches in the world have been and are formally apostate from the times of the Apostles onward, since in them the word of God has been preached in no other way. Our author may argue this lightly and without any effort at proof, but to me, and surely to all Christians, it is too dreadful to hear, so that nothing could be more of an argument against it than that such a claim should be made at all. It is true that the Antichristian apostasy has occupied a large part of the world and for a long time; but nevertheless there have always been, here and there in the East and in the West, Churches, assemblies and faithful people who have thought otherwise in every age and have kept the sacred truth. To say so, and so easily, that all the Churches without exception have been apostate from all antiquity!

units.la: Quid in Cappadocia, ubi tot quingentos simul,Nisi bebes machæra foret, uno ictu occideres.
units.tr: What would you do in Cappadocia, where you could kill so many hundreds at a single blow, if you had no sword?

units.la: VII Argum. Ergo, quotquot hactenus vixerunt uspiam fideles, pii, Christiani, extra Ecclesiam degerunt, sub horribili apostasia semper, atque ira & indignatione Dei gravissima. Quam miserè decepti, qui in Ecclesia se natos opinati fuerunt, & vivere; atque etiam, in quo non minimam felicitatis suæ collocabant partem, denique mori: sed omnium miserrimè, & inexplicabili stoliditate aut insaniâ delusi, qui non in Ecclesiâ, sed & pro ea mortem avidissimè ac certatim operierunt. Tantillo tibi omnes martyres, fideles omnes, ut quum illi piissimè se putarint egisse ac obdormivisse in sinu matris Ecclesiæ, tu eam nevidisse quidem illos afferere audeas, & sub apostasiâ, ac pro eâ mortuos, non verò, quod illi putarunt, pro Ecclesiâ ψυχή & μάρτυς.
units.tr: VII Argument.
